changes.security_impact: High sensitivity: must restrict domains and sanitize extracted data. No credential handling unless a secure session system exists.
depends_on: A sandboxed browser runtime and orchestrator support for provisioning it.
Logging/receipts for actions and extracted outputs.

changes.change: Make relay-realtime perform a live reachability preflight before dispatching any Mac UI action, cache the result for the short session, and turn downstream no-op/success-shaped receipts into a spoken, typed outcome: executed, queued, unavailable, or unverified. When Accessibility or Screen Recording is false, automatically choose browser/shell alternatives only when they are semantically equivalent; otherwise tell the owner the exact missing reachability and preserve the request for later retry rather than claiming success.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can be away from the Mac and currently may hear that an action succeeded even when the Mac cannot control its UI. They get an honest answer and a useful fallback instead of believing a reminder, message, or browser change happened when it did not.
changes.effort: Medium: add a preflight adapter over /ops/status and /observe, normalize receipts in the relay, teach mac-planner to declare equivalence/fallbacks, and add regression cases for Accessibility=false, Screen Recording=false, browser-only success, and shell success.
changes.risk: A stale preflight could incorrectly avoid a newly available route, or an over-eager fallback could perform a different operation. Use a short TTL, include the observed timestamp in the spoken result, and require semantic equivalence from the planner; recovery is retry after the next preflight.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one small status request per session or after a reachability error. No hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms on the first Mac-directed turn; subsequent turns use the short-lived cached status.
changes.security_impact: Improves security truthfulness by preventing false completion claims. It does not add a permission gate or reduce the owner’s maximum-access policy; it only reports actual reachability.
depends_on: mac-planner exposes an explicit fallback/equivalence field and committed-step receipt
Relay can read the existing /ops/status and /observe responses from the Mac bridge

changes.change: Publish a relay-side capabilities endpoint (e.g., GET /capabilities) and a durable intent/job ledger for the relay surface, mirroring what the Mac agent exposes. Include tool availability (implemented vs schema-only), route inventory, and a job/status log that downstream and faculty agents can read.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: It reduces silent failures and confusion. When the owner asks “did that work?” the system can answer reliably, even if the Mac is asleep, and developers can see what the relay can actually do without guessing.
changes.effort: Medium. Add a small router module and persistence via Durable Object or KV; write adapters to record tool calls and job receipts.
changes.risk: Low. Main risk is leaking sensitive metadata in logs; mitigate with redaction and access control.
changes.cost_impact: Low ongoing cost; storage for compact job records. Occasional writes per routed intent.
changes.latency_impact: Minimal; reads should be fast and local to the worker.
changes.security_impact: Positive if done right: better auditability. Needs strict scoping so only authorized agents read logs.

changes.change: Add a durable cross-surface evidence-and-commit protocol: every browser observation is emitted as a small signed typed fact (source session/tab, timestamp, selector or page reference, value hash, freshness), and every dependent Mac action must reference the fact ids it consumed. The relay creates one workflow id, streams stage progress, and writes a single joined receipt; if a fact expires or differs at commit time, the workflow reports a checkpoint instead of applying a stale mutation. This is orchestration and data binding between existing routes, not another action broker or approval gate.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can safely say one sentence such as “look up my latest booking and put it in Calendar” without manually relaying details between the browser and Mac, while retaining an understandable explanation of exactly which browser facts caused which Mac changes.
changes.effort: Medium-high: define schemas, persistence and freshness rules; adapt browser extraction, planner inputs, Mac action receipts, relay progress events, and dashboard rendering; add crash/reconnect tests across both downstream agents.
changes.risk: A partial failure could leave the Mac change applied while the browser workflow is incomplete. Recovery is an idempotency key plus compensating action metadata and a clear “applied/unknown/not applied” state; never silently retry a non-idempotent Mac mutation.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and Worker CPU; one additional cheap planner/evidence-normalization turn per workflow, with no extra realtime-model call unless the owner asks a follow-up.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.5–2 seconds for evidence normalization and receipt persistence; downstream browser/Mac latency remains the dominant factor.
changes.security_impact: Improves provenance and limits data transfer to selected typed facts, but introduces sensitive cross-device correlation records. Encrypt/expire evidence, scope facts to the workflow, and avoid retaining raw authenticated page content.
depends_on: A durable workflow record and reconnectable event stream on the relay
Typed browser extraction results with stable source references
Mac actions accepting idempotency keys and evidence references
A unified receipt schema across browser and Mac

changes.change: Implement an owner-scoped live target registry and resolver between relay speech and existing browser/Mac tools. A registry entry stores an alias, surface, stable session/app identity, account label hash, last-seen time, and reachability—not credentials or page content. At invocation, resolve by exact owner alias plus current reachability/freshness; if more than one target survives, return a one-sentence clarification rather than silently selecting. Emit the resolved target id into the existing job and receipt records.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can speak naturally from anywhere (“check work inbox” or “put that in calendar”) and receive an honest indication of which authenticated surface was used, without repeatedly navigating or exposing account details aloud.
changes.effort: Medium: registry schema and CRUD, browser-session and Mac-status adapters, resolver tests for stale/duplicate targets, and small pendant/dashboard create-forget-confirm flows.
changes.risk: A stale alias could direct work to the wrong account or app. Mitigate with freshness and account-label matching, explicit conflict responses, reversible alias deletion, and recording the target in receipts for recovery.
changes.cost_impact: Low storage/CPU and no recurring model cost for exact matches; occasional clarification adds one realtime turn.
changes.latency_impact: Typically tens of milliseconds for lookup plus existing reachability checks; conflict handling adds one conversational turn.
changes.security_impact: Reduces accidental broad context transfer, but creates metadata linking aliases to accounts. Encrypt or hash account labels, limit registry visibility to the owner, and expire unreachable browser targets unless pinned by the owner.
depends_on: A durable owner/session identity on the relay
A stable browser session/tab identity exposed by browser sessions
Mac app identity and reachability in get_mac_status
Receipt/job records accepting resolved target ids

changes.change: Build a read-only situational-truth fan-in service keyed by correlation ID. On a voice request, it concurrently snapshots /machine-context, /ops/status, browser inspections/session metadata, and Mac status; normalizes each observation into {source, scope, observedAt, expiresAt, value, confidence, redactions}; computes contradictions without silently choosing one; sends the compact evidence set to faculty-perception, then faculty-judgement returns a ranked answer and explicit unknowns. Store the source references and resolution in a short-lived audit record that relay-realtime can turn into a spoken brief.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner is away from the Mac, they get a dependable answer about what is really open, current, or available instead of an overconfident answer assembled from stale browser titles, old machine context, or a disconnected Mac. It prevents acting on the wrong authenticated tab while remaining entirely read-only.
changes.effort: Medium: one relay integration endpoint, a small evidence schema/TTL store, concurrent adapters for existing status routes, and perception/judgement prompt contracts. Add fixture tests for stale, missing, and contradictory sources.
changes.risk: A source can fail or leak more content than intended; fail closed to “unknown” for missing evidence, redact URLs/query strings and page text by policy, bound payload size, and retain only hashes plus selected fields. Recovery is simply retrying the snapshot with a new correlation ID; no Mac or browser mutations occur.
changes.cost_impact: No new paid service. One compact background perception call and one judgement call per request; typed deltas and source hashes reduce repeated context. Short-lived records have negligible storage cost.
changes.latency_impact: Parallel collection should add about 0.5–2 seconds, with an immediate spoken acknowledgement while reconciliation runs. Slow or offline surfaces are reported as stale rather than holding the voice channel indefinitely.
changes.security_impact: Read-only least-data projection between browser/Mac and relay; authenticated browser content never gets copied wholesale. Correlation records must have owner-scoped access and automatic expiry.
depends_on: A shared evidence-envelope schema and freshness policy
A relay fan-in route able to read existing /ops/status, /machine-context, and browser inspection/session routes
Faculty-perception and faculty-judgement contracts for contradiction reporting
A compact spoken-citation renderer in relay-realtime

changes.change: Add a read-only active-context snapshot endpoint on the Mac that atomically returns the frontmost app/window, accessibility tree summary, and a privacy-filtered downsampled screenshot or OCR regions, with capture timestamp and an explicit unavailable reason. Keep raw pixels local; expose only the selected window and structured findings to the relay’s correlation ID. Do not enable clicking or typing as part of this change.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask the pendant what is currently on the unattended Mac and get an honest answer that includes native apps and dialogs, not just whichever browser tab happens to report metadata. It also gives the hive a reliable visual source when browser and Mac status disagree.
changes.effort: Medium: implement a read-only harness adapter, active-window selection, redaction/cropping, bounded screenshot transport, and tests for Accessibility/Screen Recording being false. The current Mac reports those permissions false, so installation must surface the exact missing permission and degrade cleanly.
changes.risk: Screens can contain highly sensitive data or the wrong monitor. Never capture background windows, cap image size, redact password fields, expire payloads, and return unavailable rather than guessing when permissions or focus are ambiguous. No mutation path is added.
changes.cost_impact: Small implementation/storage cost; vision inference becomes the recurring cost only when the owner asks. Cropping and OCR reduce transfer and token cost.
changes.latency_impact: Target 1–3 seconds for capture and serialization; vision interpretation adds several seconds. Immediate spoken acknowledgement handles the wait.
changes.security_impact: New screen-data surface is sensitive. Owner-scoped authentication, in-memory processing, no durable raw screenshots, audit hashes only, and strict TTL are required.
depends_on: macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording permission or an approved alternative capture mechanism
Read-only mac-vision loop (currently disabled)
Shared evidence envelope/fan-in integration
Redaction policy for screen and OCR output

changes.change: Add a durable browser command queue with typed results and provenance (tabId, URL, timestamp, DOM locator) and support for server_browser_actions fallback when the Mac is offline.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Browser automation becomes trustworthy and resilient; tasks can continue even if the Mac sleeps.
changes.effort: High: queue, result typing, provenance, retries, and Cloudflare Browser Run integration.
changes.risk: Automation could drift on page changes; mitigate with typed extraction and explicit irreversible checkpoints.
changes.cost_impact: Moderate; dominated by browser runtime and extraction tokens.
changes.latency_impact: Queueing adds delay but enables reliability and parallelism.
changes.security_impact: Strong isolation for public browsing; strict handling of authenticated sessions; never exfiltrate secrets.
depends_on: server_browser_actions implementation
session binding in browser harness

changes.change: Implement relay_route_intent and relay_job_status as real endpoints backed by the relay’s job/history store, with a minimal envelope for intent, target, and correlation id. Add spoken status output passthrough to avoid wording drift.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant can hand tasks off reliably and later report exactly what happened, without guessing or rephrasing. That’s trust, in the owner’s ear.
changes.effort: Medium: define storage schema, wire to existing job records, add correlation and indexing.
changes.risk: Misrouting could start the wrong task; mitigate with target validation and conservative defaults. Status mismatch could mislead; mitigate by requiring receipts and never upgrading status text.
changes.cost_impact: Low per call; storage growth proportional to jobs and receipts.
changes.latency_impact: Fast intent routing; status reads should be instant.
changes.security_impact: Ensure job records do not leak sensitive content; store references and hashes where possible.
depends_on: relay has access to job store (D1) and receipt linkage from downstream

changes.change: Build a durable authenticated browser job runner that can execute typed actions (navigate, read, extract, fill) with tab/session affinity, idempotency keys, and typed results, plus a semantic diff layer for page-change detection.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: This makes ‘handle it and show me’ actually work across sessions, so the owner isn’t redoing work every time the browser reconnects.
changes.effort: High: requires queueing, persistence, and careful session binding.
changes.risk: Authenticated automation risks unintended actions; keep irreversible steps as drafts requiring approval and require provenance for all extracted data.
changes.cost_impact: Moderate; dominated by browser automation time and storage for results.
changes.latency_impact: Slightly higher, but predictable and resumable.
changes.security_impact: Keep credentials confined to the local browser/session; never ship secrets to relay logs.
depends_on: session binding and receipt capture in browser bridge
reliable command queue semantics

changes.change: Add a ‘spoken preview’ contract: before any irreversible action, generate a concise, evidence-backed spoken summary with before/after fields and a confirmation token the owner can reference (“approve with token 7Y2”).
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Prevents accidental changes while still letting the system do real prep work. It’s confidence you can hear.
changes.effort: Medium: requires standardizing receipts and generating previews from typed results.
changes.risk: If previews are wrong, the owner could approve a bad change; mitigate by requiring provenance snippets and hashes.
changes.cost_impact: Low to moderate; preview generation is cheap relative to automation.
changes.latency_impact: Minimal; preview generation happens after drafting.
changes.security_impact: Previews must avoid reading aloud sensitive data unless explicitly allowed; redact by default.
depends_on: typed results and provenance from browser/mac actions
receipt chain available to relay

changes.change: Implement relay_route_intent as the canonical routing path from speech to downstream agents, with structured fields for intent, utterance, and target, plus a mapping to existing tool calls.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: More reliable, faster routing means fewer misfires and less repetition when they ask for something by voice.
changes.effort: Medium; map intents to existing mac_run_actions/mac_delegate/browser_run_actions and record routing decisions for debugging.
changes.risk: Misrouting could trigger the wrong action. Mitigate with conservative defaults and a safe fallback to clarification.
changes.cost_impact: Low; a small routing layer. Main cost is logging/telemetry.
changes.latency_impact: Improves latency by reducing planning overhead and retries.
changes.security_impact: Routing metadata may include sensitive text; log minimally and protect records.
depends_on: A defined intent taxonomy and mapping to existing tool calls
Implementing the relay_route_intent backend handler

changes.change: Add a tiered summarization path: relay extracts minimal content, then a cheaper model summarizes, and only complex decisions escalate to a more capable model.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They get fast summaries without paying the latency cost of a top-tier model for routine tasks.
changes.effort: Low to medium; requires a summarization service and clear escalation rules.
changes.risk: Over-summarization could omit important details. Provide a way to ask for more detail or source quotes.
changes.cost_impact: Reduces per-task cost by defaulting to cheaper models.
changes.latency_impact: Improves average response time; keeps realtime free for conversation.
changes.security_impact: Summaries may expose sensitive content; keep citations and avoid storing raw data unnecessarily.
depends_on: A summarization endpoint/service and policy for escalation thresholds

changes.change: Add a pendant-side transaction control channel over the live USB serial link: a short button press emits cancel-current-job, a double press emits repeat-last-status, and a long press emits emergency-stop; the relay maps these to the active Mac/browser job by correlation id and returns a distinct LED pattern for acknowledged, cancelled, and link-lost states. Preserve the event locally until an acknowledgement arrives so a press while the relay is briefly unavailable is not silently lost.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: With no screen and often no free hands, the owner gets a physical way to stop a runaway action or ask what happened without speaking a full sentence. It is especially valuable for an unattended Mac action and is testable immediately while both chips are USB-connected.
changes.effort: Medium: nRF9160 button debouncing/state machine and LED patterns, ESP32/serial forwarding, relay correlation and job cancellation/status hooks, plus an end-to-end harness test.
changes.risk: A false press could cancel useful work; require a long press for emergency-stop and make cancellation idempotent. If serial framing breaks, fall back to current voice behavior and show link-lost LED; never infer success without relay acknowledgement.
changes.cost_impact: No API cost; negligible firmware CPU/RAM and under 1 mA transient LED/button activity. Engineering cost is the serial protocol and tests.
changes.latency_impact: Local button acknowledgement under 100 ms; relay action bounded by existing job cancellation/status latency.
changes.security_impact: The physical pendant becomes an authenticated control surface. Bind events to the paired device/session and reject stale correlation ids; emergency-stop should not expose task contents over serial.
depends_on: A relay event endpoint that accepts device-originated button events
A durable active-job correlation map shared by voice, Mac, and browser work
Firmware serial framing and acknowledgement support on the currently connected nRF9160/ESP32 pair

changes.change: Implement relay_route_intent as a real routing endpoint that validates intents, writes a durable job record, and forwards to mac_delegate or browser_run_actions when appropriate.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They get consistent behavior: their spoken request reliably becomes a tracked job with a status they can ask about later.
changes.effort: Medium to high; needs schema enforcement, durable storage, and integration tests.
changes.risk: Routing bugs could mis-send tasks; mitigate with receipts and a safe default fallback.
changes.cost_impact: Low per request; dominated by downstream work.
changes.latency_impact: Small overhead for validation and persistence.
changes.security_impact: Needs strict auth and input validation to prevent cross-tenant routing issues.
depends_on: Durable job runner

changes.change: Add a lightweight scheduler (cron/alarm) for periodic tasks like daily briefing, page-watch checks, and cleanup jobs, with clear receipts of what ran.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Features like daily briefings and watches only exist if the system can run later without them asking.
changes.effort: Medium; could use Cloudflare Cron/Durable Object alarms.
changes.risk: Misfires or duplicate runs; mitigate with idempotency keys and logs.
changes.cost_impact: Low to moderate; depends on cadence and workload.
changes.latency_impact: No impact on conversational latency.
changes.security_impact: Needs strict scoping so scheduled jobs only access allowed sessions and data.

changes.change: Add a hardware secure element to the pendant and ESP32 bridge, with device-unique keys and signed challenge-response over both USB serial links. Bind each voice event, button event, and relay push to a short-lived sequence number; have the relay and Mac reject replayed or forged events and expose the verified device identity in the spoken receipt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets confidence that a command came from their worn device and not a stale serial packet, a cloned bridge, or a misrouted browser session. This matters especially when the pendant can operate the Mac while the owner is away from it.
changes.effort: Moderate PCB respin and firmware/relay protocol work; provision keys during assembly, implement rotation/revocation, and add a recovery flow for a replaced pendant.
changes.risk: Key loss could strand the device, and clock/sequence bugs could reject legitimate commands. Provide monotonic counters, a device-repair enrollment path, and a clearly audible degraded-security state rather than silently accepting unsigned traffic.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $0.50–$2 per device plus provisioning/PCB work; negligible per-request API cost and low power draw during signing.
changes.latency_impact: Typically under 20 ms per event for signing/verification, below conversational latency.
changes.security_impact: Private keys never leave hardware; raw audio remains unaffected. The relay must not treat a valid device signature as authorization for every high-impact action—identity and action policy remain separate, with no surprise confirmation gate for ordinary reversible actions.
depends_on: A versioned signed-event envelope shared by pendant, bridge, relay, and Mac
Firmware monotonic-counter persistence across reboot
Relay and Mac verification plus device revocation/status endpoints

changes.change: Add a cross-surface device presence and custody channel: signed pendant/bridge presence events from the Mac when USB is attached, plus relay-visible TTL capsules for tasks that require the device to be present.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Tasks that need the pendant (audio tests, playback, button interactions) won’t fail mysteriously; they run only when the device is actually available.
changes.effort: Medium. Requires signing, event propagation, and TTL handling.
changes.risk: If presence lies, the system will misbehave. Use signatures and short expiries; fall back to asking the owner to reconnect.
changes.cost_impact: Low runtime overhead; some engineering across Mac and relay.
changes.latency_impact: Small; presence checks should be cached and quick.
changes.security_impact: Presence becomes a control signal; must be authenticated and tamper-resistant.
depends_on: Mac-side presence daemon and serial detection
Relay event ingestion route and verification

changes.change: Add a local audio self-test mode: generate a known tone or spoken test pattern, loop it through the mic/codec/bridge path, and report counters (packet loss, underruns, decode failures) without sending real user audio.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can confirm the hardware path works before a call, preventing confusing failures.
changes.effort: Medium. Requires audio generation, loopback plumbing, and counter reporting.
changes.risk: Could interfere with normal capture if it fails to exit cleanly. Use a clear state machine and timeout.
changes.cost_impact: Minimal compute; no extra components. Some firmware complexity and testing time.
changes.latency_impact: A few seconds to run; negligible otherwise.
changes.security_impact: Safer than using live audio. Only synthetic signals and counters are transmitted.
depends_on: A diagnostics reporting channel from device to relay
USB commissioning/calibration flow on the Mac bridge

changes.change: Add a low-power bone-conduction or open-ear earpiece path to the ESP32 audio bridge, with a hardware mute/arming switch and independent volume control, while retaining the existing pendant speaker path for ordinary replies. The relay should advertise the output channel and privacy state to downstream agents.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner could receive private answers, warnings, and meeting assistance while walking or talking to other people without broadcasting the pendant's response or reaching for a phone. They could still use the existing speaker when privacy is not needed.
changes.effort: Prototype with a BLE bone-conduction module or wired transducer, add bridge codec routing and a small authenticated channel-state message; then validate intelligibility and battery impact in real wear tests.
changes.risk: BLE pairing loss or acoustic leakage could make the owner miss a response. Recover by falling back to the existing speaker and a distinct LED pattern; never silently assume the private channel is working.
changes.cost_impact: Approximately $20–$80 for a prototype transducer/module, plus bridge firmware work. Expect tens of mW while active and negligible draw while muted; exact draw requires measuring the chosen part.
changes.latency_impact: Adds under 100 ms of local audio routing latency; no model/API cost.
changes.security_impact: A new wireless audio endpoint creates a pairing and eavesdropping surface. Use authenticated bonding, explicit mute state, and do not transmit private audio until the endpoint confirms encryption and readiness.
depends_on: ESP32 bridge firmware must expose authenticated output-channel state
Relay audio pipeline must select output per utterance and know whether the private path is confirmed
A physical arming/mute gesture must be defined for the one-button pendant

changes.change: Add presence-aware session handoff: relay tracks device availability and last successful step, then resumes on another surface (Mac, browser, relay) when one goes offline.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Tasks don’t die when the Mac sleeps or the pendant disconnects. The system continues from where it left off, or tells the owner what’s blocking.
changes.effort: High: needs shared state, idempotent steps, and resumable workflows.
changes.risk: State divergence between surfaces. Mitigate with receipts, job IDs, and explicit step checkpoints.
changes.cost_impact: Moderate; includes state storage and additional coordination calls.
changes.latency_impact: Adds small overhead to coordination; improves perceived reliability.
changes.security_impact: Shared state must be access-controlled; store only what’s necessary.
depends_on: Durable job runner or equivalent resumable workflow support
Presence/sequence tracking across relay and Mac

changes.change: On the pendant, add a low-power ‘task heartbeat’ LED pattern and a single-button status query: short press asks relay for the current job status and speaks a brief update if the audio path is available.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets immediate reassurance without opening anything: heartbeat means ‘working’, solid means ‘waiting’, quick press gets a spoken status.
changes.effort: Medium: firmware skill, relay endpoint, and a tiny status protocol.
changes.risk: LED meanings could confuse; keep patterns minimal and documented. Audio path failures must fall back to LED only.
changes.cost_impact: Low; minor firmware work and negligible power if implemented as brief periodic blink.
changes.latency_impact: Instant visual feedback; status query depends on relay reachability.
changes.security_impact: No sensitive content; status only.
depends_on: Device skill for button-to-status request
A relay endpoint to answer status from job records

changes.change: Add a tiny low-power vibration motor and driver to the pendant, with firmware patterns for acknowledgement, urgent result, failure, and incoming completion. Expose a relay command that can request a pattern with a correlation id, and queue at most one completion pattern while the link is down.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can know that a spoken request completed or failed without staring at the pendant or keeping audio enabled. This makes unattended, pocketed, or noisy use dependable and gives the wearable a private notification channel instead of relying on the single LED.
changes.effort: Moderate hardware revision and enclosure change: motor, transistor/driver, flyback protection, firmware PWM pattern table, and relay delivery semantics. Prototype can be wired onto the currently USB-connected nRF9160 pendant before a board revision.
changes.risk: Added vibration and current spikes could reset the modem or shorten battery life; rate-limit patterns, budget peak current, and fall back to LED/audio. A stuck driver needs thermal/current protection. Recovery is firmware-safe default-off and a physical disconnect option.
changes.cost_impact: Approximately $1–$3 in components and under 20 mA peak while vibrating; negligible API cost because patterns are tiny events.
changes.latency_impact: Local acknowledgement under 100 ms when USB/LTE link is live; queued completion may be delayed until reconnect.
changes.security_impact: Patterns must not encode sensitive content; only generic states and opaque correlation ids should cross the device link.
depends_on: A reliable pendant event/push transport over the present USB serial connection
Firmware event queue and modem/USB power-budget measurement
Relay correlation of long-running Mac/browser jobs to device notifications

changes.change: Route long-running monitoring, research, and summarization tasks to cheaper background models, with the relay acting only as a conversational front door and notification presenter.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Keeps voice interactions snappy and reliable while still enabling richer capabilities without burning budget.
changes.effort: Medium to high. Needs a task taxonomy, routing rules, and receipts for results.
changes.risk: Misrouted tasks could be slow or incomplete. Mitigate with receipts and fallback to Mac delegation.
changes.cost_impact: Potentially large savings by avoiding expensive realtime usage for background work.
changes.latency_impact: Improves voice latency; background tasks become less jittery with proper queues.
changes.security_impact: Ensure data minimization and strict scoping when tasks leave the device.
depends_on: A queue/scheduler and status reporting across surfaces.

changes.change: Introduce a spoken 'session mode' with explicit start/stop commands and scoped permissions (e.g., 'monitor my email for 30 minutes'), plus a one-button pendant stop that always cancels the session.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Gives the owner confidence and control: they know what’s being watched, for how long, and how to stop it instantly.
changes.effort: Medium. Needs UX rules, session state, and consistent cancellation semantics across surfaces.
changes.risk: If stop fails, the system could keep monitoring. Mitigate with timeouts and kill-switch precedence.
changes.cost_impact: Low to moderate. Mostly state management and messaging.
changes.latency_impact: Minimal for voice; monitoring latency depends on downstream surfaces.
changes.security_impact: Strongly positive: explicit consent boundaries and easy revocation.
depends_on: Session state shared between relay and devices, and a notification channel.

changes.change: Add a low-power coin vibration motor and a protected driver to the nRF9160 pendant, with firmware patterns for acknowledgement, private notification, urgent stop, and recording-active status. Keep the existing LED as a secondary visual indicator rather than the only output.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can receive and control the assistant silently in public, in a pocket, or where speech is impossible. Distinct tactile patterns make it possible to know whether a command started, finished, failed, or is still recording without looking at the pendant.
changes.effort: Hardware spin for a tiny motor, transistor/driver, and board routing; firmware event-pattern table; relay event mapping; enclosure and battery testing.
changes.risk: Motor noise may be audible and vibration can annoy the wearer; provide intensity limits and a disable pattern. Added current can shorten battery life. Recovery is to fall back to LED/audio and expose battery-aware pattern selection.
changes.cost_impact: Approximately $1–$4 in component and assembly cost per unit, plus a few mA only while pulsing; no model/API cost.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-100 ms local feedback for button and link events; no added conversational latency.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy by reducing required speech, but patterns must not encode sensitive content. Firmware update must be signed and pairing state preserved.
depends_on: A defined pendant event vocabulary shared with the relay
A device-authenticated command channel for relay-to-pendant pushes
Battery and enclosure validation

changes.change: Add a self-describing /capabilities endpoint for the relay surface, including granted tools, available routes, and current wiring status (implemented vs schema-only).
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Faster diagnosis when something fails. The assistant can tell the owner what’s actually possible right now instead of guessing or wasting turns.
changes.effort: Medium: add route, hook into build metadata, expose wiring flags.
changes.risk: Low. Risk is leaking internal details; mitigate by returning only capability names and statuses, not secrets.
changes.cost_impact: Low per call; small maintenance cost.
changes.latency_impact: Negligible.
changes.security_impact: Ensure output is sanitized and excludes tokens, session identifiers, and private config.

changes.change: Implement relay_route_intent as the explicit routing path from realtime to mac-planner/mac-vision, with status callbacks and a durable intent id.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Natural voice commands reliably land on the right agent, and the owner can ask what happened without re-explaining.
changes.effort: High: needs backend wiring, intent id propagation, and job record linkage.
changes.risk: Medium. Misrouting would be confusing; include clear fallback to mac_delegate when ambiguous.
changes.cost_impact: Low per intent; main cost is development and testing.
changes.latency_impact: Small overhead; reduces costly retries.
changes.security_impact: Log intent metadata only; avoid storing raw utterances unless needed for debugging and explicitly allowed.

changes.change: Implement server_browser_actions using an isolated, ephemeral browser session with strict allowlists and artifact capture (DOM snapshot, extracted text, evidence links).
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Lets tasks continue even when the Mac is offline, and gives verifiable results the owner can trust.
changes.effort: High: needs Browser Run integration, session isolation, and evidence capture.
changes.risk: High. Browser automation can leak credentials or take unintended actions; enforce allowlists and read-only modes by default.
changes.cost_impact: Moderate per run; dominated by cloud browser time.
changes.latency_impact: Higher than local actions; acceptable for unattended workflows.
changes.security_impact: Strong isolation, no credential reuse across tasks, explicit user authorization for write actions.

changes.change: Add a physical conversational checkpoint protocol: after the relay hands a multi-surface task to Mac or browser, it emits a compact spoken 'contract' (goal, scope, expected artifact, and expiration), accepts a single spoken correction during a short grace window, and otherwise lets the downstream plan continue. The contract and correction become immutable metadata on the resulting receipt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can correct a misunderstood request while walking away without repeating the entire task, while still knowing exactly what the remote agents were told to do. This is materially safer and more usable than silent handoff or a long clarification dialogue.
changes.effort: Medium-high: relay session state, audio playback/interruption handling, downstream request metadata, and receipt display all need coordinated changes.
changes.risk: A late correction could race an action already executed. Use monotonic request versions, stop accepting corrections once execution begins, and clearly speak when the window closes; recover by issuing a compensating action or undo where available.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible model cost; one extra short response per delegated task. Storage is tiny per request.
changes.latency_impact: Adds 1–3 seconds only when the owner chooses to correct; normal delegation remains immediate.
changes.security_impact: Improves transparency but places task scope in receipts. Encrypt or minimize spoken contract metadata and never include secrets from browser pages.
depends_on: A durable request/job identity shared by relay, Mac planner, and browser command queue
A pendant audio interruption or short-grace playback mechanism
Receipt records that store request version and spoken correction

changes.change: Add a cross-surface sensitive-content guardian: before any Mac screenshot, browser extraction, or spoken readback is sent through the relay, mac-vision and the browser extension classify visible regions as password/OTP/payment/health/private-message content. Replace those regions with typed placeholders and attach a sensitivity manifest to the evidence/job receipt; the owner can say 'include the hidden field' to request an explicit one-shot reveal bound to the current session.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can safely use the pendant around real work and authenticated sites without choosing between useful remote help and accidentally broadcasting a password or private message. It preserves task control while making the dangerous parts obvious in the spoken response.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared redaction schema across Mac screenshots, browser DOM extraction, audio narration, and receipt storage; adversarial tests for OCR and DOM leaks.
changes.risk: False negatives could leak sensitive text; false positives could make a task frustrating. Recover with visible/ spoken placeholders, a per-session audit trail, and explicit one-shot reveal rather than silently disabling the whole workflow.
changes.cost_impact: Small per-request classifier/token cost; roughly $0.005-$0.02 for OCR/DOM sensitivity checks, with no new hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds about 100-400 ms for DOM checks and lightweight OCR; full-screen vision may add 1-2 seconds only when a screenshot is requested.
changes.security_impact: Strongly improves data minimization, but the classifier itself sees the raw content locally. Keep classification on the Mac/extension, transmit only redacted artifacts and sensitivity labels, and expire reveal artifacts immediately.
depends_on: mac-vision screenshot and region metadata
browser extension DOM extraction with field labels
relay evidence bundles and job receipts
a session-scoped spoken one-shot reveal command

changes.change: Add a low-power coin vibration motor and a single capacitive touch strip to the nRF9160 pendant enclosure, driven by a tiny local event queue. Use distinct short patterns for listening, Mac job accepted, job finished, and sensitive-content redaction; use touch-and-hold as a local cancel/mute gesture while the Mac or relay is acting.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets private, glance-free confirmation and an immediate escape hatch in a noisy room or meeting, without waiting for speech or looking at an LED. This makes long-running cross-device work usable while walking away from the Mac.
changes.effort: Moderate enclosure/PCB revision and firmware event protocol; validate motor current against the existing battery and USB tethered test setup before enabling LTE use.
changes.risk: Motor noise can contaminate the microphone and added draw can reduce battery life. Isolate it mechanically, suppress microphone capture during vibration, cap duty cycle, and fall back to the existing LED/button when power is low.
changes.cost_impact: Approximately $2-$8 in components plus enclosure/PCB work; roughly 10-30 mA only during a vibration pulse, negligible average draw with a duty-cycle cap.
changes.latency_impact: Local acknowledgement under 50 ms; no relay round trip for cancel/mute.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy by providing local mute/cancel feedback; touch events must be debounced and authenticated to the paired session so an accidental touch cannot trigger an unintended workflow.
depends_on: Pendant firmware local event queue
relay/mac job lifecycle events
USB serial hardware test harness
audio bridge microphone mute control

changes.change: Add an end-to-end audio diagnostic handshake: pendant emits a known marker; bridge loops it; relay verifies timing, packet loss, and codec compatibility; Mac reports device driver state if connected.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Prevents confusing failures where the assistant seems unresponsive but the audio chain is broken.
changes.effort: Medium to high; requires firmware skill, bridge command, relay verification logic, and optional Mac reporting.
changes.risk: Diagnostics could capture ambient audio. Mitigation: use synthetic markers and discard captured audio immediately.
changes.cost_impact: Moderate in bandwidth and compute during diagnostics; negligible when idle.
changes.latency_impact: Adds a few seconds only when invoked.
changes.security_impact: Keeps diagnostic data minimal and ephemeral; never store raw audio.

changes.change: Introduce a compact conversation-decision memory: store short, schema-validated summaries with TTL, sensitivity tags, and source provenance; retrieval returns only task-relevant facts.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The assistant becomes consistent and efficient, without paying to resend large context every turn.
changes.effort: Medium; requires schema, storage routes, and retrieval integration with planners.
changes.risk: Stale or incorrect summaries could mislead. Mitigation: TTLs, confidence scores, and explicit overwrite rules.
changes.cost_impact: Low; dominated by summarization/embedding if used.
changes.latency_impact: Small write/read overhead; reduces future turn latency by shrinking context.
changes.security_impact: Sensitive summaries remain scoped; avoid shipping private content to cheaper tiers unless necessary.

changes.change: Add a pendant-local privacy posture switch: a long press on the existing button toggles QUIET/PRIVATE mode, with the LED confirming the state. The relay must attach the posture to every voice run; in PRIVATE mode it may still perform Mac/browser work but returns only a generic spoken acknowledgment and places sensitive findings in a local-Mac review card. A second long press exits the mode.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can walk into a meeting or public place and immediately prevent private calendar, browser, or source details from being spoken, without finding a phone or relying on a server guess about who is listening.
changes.effort: Firmware button state and LED feedback; relay session/posture propagation; Mac dashboard card and deferred result retrieval; browser/Mac agents need a `speak_policy` field.
changes.risk: A missed or ambiguous press could leave the owner in the wrong posture. Use a distinct 1.5-second hold, LED pattern, and spoken generic confirmation only; recover by holding again. If the link drops, firmware keeps the last posture locally.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; small firmware change and a few bytes of session state.
changes.latency_impact: No meaningful added latency; posture is local and attached before transcription routing.
changes.security_impact: Improves confidentiality, but must be fail-closed for sensitive spoken output when posture is unknown or link state changes. Do not put raw private results in relay logs.
depends_on: A relay session field carrying privacy posture through /pipeline/audio, /pipeline/events, and downstream jobs
A Mac review-card/result endpoint for answers suppressed from speech
Firmware button gesture and LED state implementation

changes.change: Expose a relay-level capability inventory route (like /capabilities) and a typed intent routing endpoint that accepts an intent label and payload, logs it, and forwards to the appropriate downstream tool without the relay inventing its own protocol.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: More reliable handoffs: the owner’s requests don’t get lost or misrouted, and we can report what’s supported right now.
changes.effort: Medium: add route, schema validation, logging, and mapping to existing plan/execute paths.
changes.risk: Incorrect mappings could misroute actions. Mitigation: conservative allowlist and receipts.
changes.cost_impact: Small; mostly validation and logging.
changes.latency_impact: Minimal overhead per request.
changes.security_impact: Needs strict auth; intent payloads must be validated to prevent injection.
depends_on: Existing plan/execute infrastructure

changes.change: Add a small offline voice-note buffer and retry queue on the pendant (using microSD if available) so short captures survive LTE/USB drops and upload later with metadata (timestamp, duration, sequence).
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant becomes dependable: you can capture ideas even with spotty connectivity.
changes.effort: Medium: storage format, queue management, retry logic, and upload handshake.
changes.risk: Storage corruption or queue growth. Mitigation: bounded retention, checksums, and compaction.
changes.cost_impact: Minimal BOM change; some power/storage overhead.
changes.latency_impact: None during capture; retries happen opportunistically.
changes.security_impact: Sensitive audio at rest; should be encrypted and auto-expire.
depends_on: Capture pipeline state context
Server support for resumable uploads

changes.change: Add a low-power haptic actuator and a physical three-position privacy switch to the pendant, with firmware events for silent-alert, active-listening, and transmit-disabled states. Expose those states to the relay so every realtime workflow can fail closed when the switch is off and acknowledge urgent events without audio.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can receive a discreet alert in a noisy place and can prove—by touch—that the pendant is not listening or transmitting. This enables safe call screening, meeting capture, and future ambient workflows without forcing the owner to look at a phone or trust an invisible software state.
changes.effort: Moderate hardware revision plus GPIO/firmware driver, battery characterization, relay state propagation, and a small set of end-to-end usability tests.
changes.risk: Added power draw, enclosure changes, accidental switch movement, and new firmware states. Recover with a default-off transmit state after reboot, watchdog-safe GPIO handling, and a software diagnostic that reports physical switch position.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $2–$8 in components and assembly at prototype quantity; haptic pulses add tens of milliwatts only while active, while the switch is effectively zero draw. No meaningful API cost.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-100 ms local haptic response; relay acknowledgement remains network-dependent but is not required for privacy state enforcement.
changes.security_impact: Strongly improves privacy by making transmit disable a physical, locally enforced state; switch position must override any server command and be included in audit receipts.
depends_on: A pendant firmware event/state protocol
A relay device-presence and push channel
Audio pipeline session state propagation

pending.name: relay_route_intent
pending.why: The relay needs a safe, explicit routing tool to send normalized intents to downstream agents without inventing ad-hoc protocols in the voice path. It should encapsulate target selection, session binding, and minimal context fields, and return a job reference for status checks.

utterance.description: Raw or normalized user utterance to preserve meaning.

context.description: Optional session context such as locale, time, constraints.

target.description: Preferred downstream target agent id, e.g. 'mac-planner' or 'mac-vision'.

example_call.utterance: Open Safari and go to my inbox.

pending.expected_output: A structured response containing an accepted flag, normalized intent, resolved target, and a jobId or correlation id for later status queries. May include a spoken_reply for immediate voice feedback.

pending.name: server_browser_actions
pending.why: To do useful voice tasks when the owner’s Mac/browser is offline, the relay needs a server-side browser automation capability (Cloudflare Browser Run) for public pages. This reduces dependency on the Mac being online and avoids fragile routing through the browser extension.

actions.description: High-level browser actions to perform (navigate, click, extract, search).

pending.expected_output: A result object with a final URL, a list of step results, and extracted artifacts (text/HTML). Should include errors and timeouts in a consistent shape.

pending.name: relay_event_push
pending.why: The relay needs a way to deliver asynchronous completion updates to the pendant (or to a paired phone) after the voice session ends. Without it, users have to poll for status, which is awkward and unreliable for long-running tasks.
pending.why_existing_tools_insufficient: mac_run_actions and mac_delegate start work; relay_job_status answers only when asked. There is no implemented relay notification channel to push a completion message to the wearer when the Mac finishes a job.

jobId.description: The job to monitor for completion.

spoken.description: A short user-facing sentence to play on the pendant.

ttl_seconds.description: How long the notification should be kept if the device is offline.

example_call.spoken: The Outlook cleanup finished. I archived 12 messages and left a summary on your Mac.

pending.expected_output: Acknowledgement that the event was queued for delivery, plus a delivery status (queued/delivered/expired).

denied.summary: “Every weekday morning, check my authenticated work portal for new high-priority items and tell me only what needs my attention.”
denied.why: Not mine to claim: the core of this ask is an authenticated WORK PORTAL, and briefing.js reads Calendar/Mail/files/Notes only — it never opens a web session. The scheduling and 'only what needs my attention' filtering it shares with the briefing family are built (routines.js daily schedule + priority-vs-bulk ranking), but the portal read belongs with the browser harness (browserSessions.js/pageWatch.js). Re-file against that layer.

denied.summary: Replace FULL_CONTROL_MODE's undifferentiated execution path with a typed action broker: structured read/open/search actions by default, and separate m
denied.why: Owner policy: maximum access, no gates. Typed classification for observability is welcome; blocking is not.

denied.summary: Put a typed capability broker in front of the existing FULL_CONTROL computer loop. Accept structured argv/files/app/UI operations with per-capability
denied.why: Owner policy: maximum access, no gates. Typed classification for observability is welcome; blocking is not.

denied.summary: Add a typed action policy in front of FULL_CONTROL_MODE: classify every action as read-only, reversible local mutation, or high-impact mutation; requi
denied.why: Owner policy: maximum access, no gates. A typed action policy that requires a one-use confirmation for high-impact mutations is exactly the gate that has been rejected twice. The observability half is covered by chg-5fc73ce3 (result receipts).

denied.name: short_grace_audio_buffer
denied.what_it_does: After end-of-speech or button release, keep a short rolling buffer (e.g., 2–5 seconds) and append it if the user resumes, otherwise discard.
denied.why_not_server_side: It must work even if the link drops and should avoid uploading unnecessary audio.
denied.trigger: speech end detected; optionally button state
denied.inputs: raw mic audio frames and voice activity detection events
denied.storage: RAM ring buffer; optional transient SD cache if RAM is tight
denied.ram_budget: ~32–96 KB for compressed audio and bookkeeping; exact size depends on codec and sample rate
denied.why:
Denied — conflicts with a project constraint.

Two ways, and the second is the one that matters. First, 'optional transient SD cache if RAM is tight' writes owner audio to the card outside the upload-failure path, against the standing rule in firmware/nrf9160/src/pendant_store.h:45: 'Only save an audio copy to SD if the chunk upload cannot be uploaded. SD is the failure path, never the default.'

Second and more fundamental: the skill is defined as continuing to capture and retain the owner's speech AFTER they released the button. On this device the button release IS the end of consent — the mic is powered up on the sw0 edge and torn down on release (main.c:1598 and finish_button_press, main.c:1043). Keeping 2-5 seconds past that point, and appending it if the owner happens to resume, is the pendant deciding that the owner did not really mean to stop. That is exactly the class of behaviour this project keeps behind a deliberate physical confirmation.

The problem you are actually solving — a word clipped off the end of an utterance — is real and worth a different fix. Note that main.c:122-131 already calibrates end-of-speech thresholds against the recording's own measured noise floor, so the tuning surface exists. Propose an adjustment there, or a second press to resume the same turn, and it will not run into either constraint.

denied.name: offline_voice_note_buffer
denied.what_it_does: Record up to N short audio clips when the network is unavailable, store them encrypted on microSD, and upload when LTE-M is available.
denied.why_not_server_side: If the link drops, the server cannot capture audio; the pendant must hold it until connectivity returns.
denied.inputs: audio from I2S mic; optional spoken tag like “todo” or “idea”
denied.storage: Encrypted files on microSD; each clip <1 MB, plus a small queue index
denied.ram_budget: Small ring buffer and encoder state; aim <32 KB additional RAM
denied.why:
Denied as a duplicate. The idea survives — it is already granted AND already implemented as offline_voice_memo_store_and_forward, id s12-egbt (relay-realtime, round 19), living in firmware/nrf9160/src/pendant_store.{h,c}.

Read that header before re-proposing. pendant_store.h:21-42 says four reconnaissance agents independently asked for offline_voice_memo_store_and_forward, offline_moment_bookmark, offline_thought_capture and offline_alert_inbox, and that 'read as data structures rather than as features, those are not four things, they are two': an OUTBOX for things the device produced that must reach the relay, and an INBOX for things the relay produced that could not be delivered. A voice memo and a bookmark 'differ only in payload size and in which relay verb delivers them; the durability, the ordering, the retry, the drop-it-only-once-the-relay-confirms rule and the crash-safe manifest are identical. One queue, typed items.' Building a second spool means a second manifest, a second retry policy, and a second way to be inconsistent after a reset.

It is already constraint-clean, which is why it was accepted: it spools ONLY on upload failure. pendant_store.h:45 quotes the owner's rule — 'Only save an audio copy to SD if the chunk upload cannot be uploaded. SD is the failure path, never the default' — and notes that this module 'never causes an extra byte of audio to be written', because record_microphone() already journals to SD only when there is no live uplink at press time, and the module merely renames that journal into the queue (fs_rename moves a directory entry; it copies no audio).

Bring your additions to s12-egbt as manifest fields, not as a new mechanism.

Specific to your request: this is your own already-granted skill. s12-egbt was granted TO relay-realtime in round 19 under the name offline_voice_memo_store_and_forward, and your s12-jivd restates it in one sentence with less detail. Check granted deviceSkills before spending a round on a re-ask — describe() and the granted list both carry it.

denied.name: status_update_listener
denied.what_it_does: Listens for status updates for jobs started from the pendant and plays a short spoken update or LED pattern when a job completes, fails, or needs attention.
denied.why_not_server_side: The pendant must react even when the phone/Mac is asleep or the network is flaky; local behavior (LED, audio cues, button interactions) must be implemented on-device.
denied.trigger: server push or periodic link-layer heartbeat when connected; optional button press to cycle through pending statuses.
denied.inputs: A job id and a short status summary string provided by the relay when available.
denied.storage: Small ring buffer of pending job ids and the last status message, stored in local flash.
denied.ram_budget: Very small; keep active state to a few entries and reuse buffers to fit within constrained RAM.
denied.why:
Denied as a duplicate. The idea survives — it is already granted AND already implemented as offline_alert_inbox, id s13-369p (browser-extension, round 14): 'Receives short, prioritized alerts from the relay, queues them locally, and lets the owner press the button to play the next alert over the existing speaker. The LED indicates unread count and an error/expired state; alerts remain available across a dropped phone/Mac link.' It is the INBOX half of firmware/nrf9160/src/pendant_store.{h,c} — pendant_store_poll_alerts(), pendant_store_inbox_pending(), pendant_store_surface_inbox() — with alert text on the card and a durability requirement that survives with the radio off.

pendant_store.h:21-42 explains why there is one inbox and not several: four agents asked for four things that were really two data structures, and 'building three separate mechanisms would have meant three manifests, three retry policies and three ways to be inconsistent after a reset.' Every queue-of-things-for-the-owner in this pending set is the same structure with a different label on the payload.

There is a hard physical reason not to grant a second one: there is exactly ONE LED (led0, firmware/nrf9160/src/main.c:26, single element, no colour), and it already carries three meanings — solid means a staged reply is waiting for a play press (main.c:1092-1110), a 250 ms toggle means recording (main.c:1599-1600), and s13-369p's unread/error state. Each additional queue that wants 'distinct LED patterns' is bidding for the same one bit. Bring your urgency classes and expiry buckets to s13-369p as fields on its existing record.

Specific to your request: 'plays a short spoken update' assumes on-device text-to-speech. There is none. The pendant decodes Opus that the relay rendered and pushes it out over I2S to the ESP32 bridge (main.c:1092-1113, boards/nrf9160dk_nrf9160_ns.overlay); it cannot turn a status string into audio. So the storable artifact is either the string (which the device cannot speak) or relay-rendered audio (which cannot be kept on the card — see the standing rule at pendant_store.h:45, 'SD is the failure path, never the default'). s13-369p already resolved this correctly: the relay sends short alerts, the device queues and surfaces them, and the LED carries the count.

denied.name: completion_summary_queue
denied.what_it_does: Stores short completion summaries and a source receipt reference locally so the pendant can play them when the owner taps, even if the relay connection is spotty.
denied.why_not_server_side: It must work when the owner is moving through poor coverage and needs quick access without waiting for a round trip.
denied.trigger: button press when summaries are waiting
denied.inputs: summary text, receipt hash, timestamp, optional priority
denied.storage: small ring buffer in local storage (e.g., a few KB per item, capped at ~10 items)
denied.ram_budget: Minimal; keep only the current item in RAM and stream from storage when playing.
denied.why:
Denied as a duplicate. The idea survives — it is already granted AND already implemented as offline_alert_inbox, id s13-369p (browser-extension, round 14): 'Receives short, prioritized alerts from the relay, queues them locally, and lets the owner press the button to play the next alert over the existing speaker. The LED indicates unread count and an error/expired state; alerts remain available across a dropped phone/Mac link.' It is the INBOX half of firmware/nrf9160/src/pendant_store.{h,c} — pendant_store_poll_alerts(), pendant_store_inbox_pending(), pendant_store_surface_inbox() — with alert text on the card and a durability requirement that survives with the radio off.

pendant_store.h:21-42 explains why there is one inbox and not several: four agents asked for four things that were really two data structures, and 'building three separate mechanisms would have meant three manifests, three retry policies and three ways to be inconsistent after a reset.' Every queue-of-things-for-the-owner in this pending set is the same structure with a different label on the payload.

There is a hard physical reason not to grant a second one: there is exactly ONE LED (led0, firmware/nrf9160/src/main.c:26, single element, no colour), and it already carries three meanings — solid means a staged reply is waiting for a play press (main.c:1092-1110), a 250 ms toggle means recording (main.c:1599-1600), and s13-369p's unread/error state. Each additional queue that wants 'distinct LED patterns' is bidding for the same one bit. Bring your urgency classes and expiry buckets to s13-369p as fields on its existing record.

Specific to your request: same blocking problem as s18-i0h0. 'Stores short completion summaries... so the pendant can play them when the owner taps' requires either on-device TTS, which does not exist, or keeping relay-rendered audio on the card as routine storage, which the owner's standing rule forbids: 'Only save an audio copy to SD if the chunk upload cannot be uploaded. SD is the failure path, never the default' (pendant_store.h:45). s13-369p is the sanctioned shape of this — the relay decides what is worth saying, the device holds it and surfaces it on a press. Note also that the truthfulness property you want next to a completion summary is granted separately as truthful_action_status_beacon (mac-terminal s15-cbhs).

denied.name: uplink_health_ping
denied.what_it_does: Periodically (during an active conversation) measures uplink health using lightweight counters: packet loss, jitter proxy, and buffer underruns, and reports a compact summary to the relay.
denied.why_not_server_side: Only the pendant and its modem see real-time radio behavior and buffer states; the server can’t reliably infer it from transcript gaps alone.
denied.trigger: During an active voice session; also on button press to start a quick preflight check.
denied.inputs: Modem/network counters and audio buffer underrun events; no user content.
denied.storage: A tiny rolling window of the last few health samples (e.g., 10–20 entries) in RAM; no persistent storage required.
denied.ram_budget: Very small: a few structs and counters; well under 10 KB.
denied.why:
Denied as a duplicate. Granted once, as offline-reality-beacon, id s2-i8xy (faculty-perception, round 40), which is a superset of this: firmware build ID, boot/session ID, monotonic timestamp, WebSocket connected state, last successful relay acknowledgement, uplink/downlink packet-loss counters, audio mode and SD fallback accounting, sent on connect/reconnect and on a low-rate heartbeat.

s2-i8xy was kept because it answers the question yours does not: it lets a consumer distinguish 'last heard' from 'currently healthy'. Your version only reports during an active conversation, which means silence stays ambiguous — a healthy idle pendant and a dead one look identical. It also earned the grant by respecting the owner's storage rule without being told: 'obey the owner's rule that SD is failure-buffer-only, so do not write routinely when connected.'

Your jitter proxy and the button-triggered preflight are worth folding into s2-i8xy. Note that a preflight does not need a new gesture — s2-i8xy already carries a diagnostic request path, and USB serial is the transport that works today while LTE-M is unregistered.

args.user_asks: “Remember this exactly, and when my Mac and browser are next available, carry it out across whichever app or logged-in tab is needed; tell me on the pendant when it is actually done, and if anything is ambiguous, ask me then.”

args.user_asks: “What is on my Mac right now?” or “Read the page I left open and tell me the important parts.”

Today the relay can converse, but it cannot give a grounded, current visual state of the unattended Mac and authenticated browser as an audio answer. args.model_tier: Mac-vision captures a single current screen or selected open-tab snapshot and extracts only visible text/structure; browser-extension supplies tab URL/title and DOM text where available; a background compact model produces a short evidence-linked brief; realtime relay handles the spoken question and reads the result. args.latency_budget: Acknowledge immediately; return a basic tab/screen inventory in 2 seconds when the Mac is online, and a spoken summary in 5–10 seconds. If the Mac is offline or capture permissions are absent, say so explicitly and provide no inferred answer.

args.security_concerns: Screens may expose passwords, private messages, health data, or work secrets. Require device-bound authentication, redact password fields and known secret-like regions before model submission, send only the requested window/tab, retain no image by default, and speak a warning when the result contains potentially sensitive content. This is read-only and should not control the Mac.
missing: A read-only Mac snapshot endpoint with explicit window/tab targeting, freshness timestamp, permission-state reporting, and automatic secret-region redaction.
A browser bridge operation that returns current tab provenance plus bounded visible text, not arbitrary session cookies or hidden page data.
A mac-vision mode that can classify/describe a single snapshot without entering the disabled computer-use control loop.
A relay response schema carrying evidence references and freshness so spoken answers cannot be mistaken for current state when capture failed.
A pendant-friendly ‘repeat last snapshot’ and dashboard thumbnail/provenance view with automatic expiry.

Let the relay attach a haptic outcome to every downstream Mac/browser job receipt, while preserving the existing one-button and LED behavior as fallback.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can be away from the Mac, in a noisy place, or unable to look at the LED. They would know silently that a request was accepted or completed—and distinguish success from failure—without the device speaking private information aloud or requiring them to ask again.

args.latency_impact: No meaningful request latency; outcome acknowledgment can be delivered as soon as the relay receives a receipt, typically tens to hundreds of milliseconds.

args.user_asks: “I’m leaving now—watch this job until it finishes, recover safely if it stalls, and tell me only if I need to intervene.”
args.why_useful: The owner is physically away from the Mac much of the time. Today a voice request can start work, but nothing reliably watches a long-running Mac/browser task after the conversation ends, detects a stall, performs bounded recovery, and escalates only a genuine human decision. This turns the pendant into a useful remote presence rather than a one-shot command button.
args.model_tier: Use a durable Worker/Durable Object monitor and deterministic heartbeats/state checks for normal operation. Use a cheaper background model only to classify ambiguous failure evidence; use relay-realtime for the initial request and urgent spoken escalation.
args.latency_budget: Start acknowledgement under 1 second. Heartbeats every 15–30 seconds without model calls; detect a stall within one heartbeat window. Speak only on completion, bounded recovery, or a real intervention request.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.01–$0.05 per watched job, dominated by occasional failure classification; normal heartbeats are Worker/storage operations. Cost scales with watch duration and should have an explicit expiry.
args.security_concerns: The monitor must be scoped to the exact job and allowed recovery actions, never broaden a goal after a failure. Browser sessions and Mac files remain private to their surfaces; send the relay only status summaries and evidence links. Record every recovery and provide an undo/stop command from the pendant.
missing: A durable watch/heartbeat and expiry facility on the relay (Cron/Durable Object alarm or equivalent)
Typed progress and failure signals from Mac planner, Mac vision, and browser extension
A bounded recovery policy with retry budgets and stop/undo semantics
Pendant push delivery for completion and escalation after the original voice turn

transcript.text:
Recorded two new capabilities:

1. **Return-to-work delta and context restoration** — compare the Mac and authenticated browser state with a departure checkpoint, explain meaningful changes, and restore the owner’s prior working context.

2. **Unattended job babysitting** — monitor a Mac/browser task while the owner is away, detect stalls, perform bounded recovery, and notify the pendant only on completion or when human intervention is needed.

The activity-ledger proposal was rejected as already covered by the backlog, so I did not count it as new.

The main remaining requirements are durable relay monitoring, cross-surface progress signals, resumable Mac/browser control, and pendant push notifications.
I’ll quickly map what’s available now, then I’ll flag any gaps that still need a new tool, device skill, or context.

args.why_useful: Today the pendant is a low-latency front door, but once it hands work to a planner or browser queue the owner has no reliable conversational interrupt or amendment path. args.change: Add a speculative, cancelable intent race for spoken requests: the relay emits a normalized utterance plus a stable request ID to a tiny local classifier immediately, while mac-planner/browser planning starts in parallel only when the utterance is plausibly actionable. The first authoritative result wins; late results are discarded by request ID. If confidence is low or the owner interrupts, the relay cancels the downstream work and keeps the turn conversational. args.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant feels immediate even when LTE-M or the Mac is slow: simple questions get a fast answer, while complex requests are already being prepared. This gives the owner a cited, read-only cross-surface comparison from a worn pendant, useful while away from the Mac and without exposing browser credentials to the relay model.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background planner for source-specific extraction and deterministic comparison; realtime only acknowledges the request and reads the final concise delta. mac-vision is used only when a browser page cannot provide structured extraction.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge immediately; return a first partial result within 5 s and the complete comparison within 20 s for up to two Mac sources and two already-open authenticated tabs. If one surface is offline, report that source as unavailable rather than guessing.

args.security_concerns: The relay must receive only normalized fields, hashes, and source citations—not cookies, passwords, or unrestricted page dumps. Read-only mode must be enforced at the executor, not merely promised in the prompt.

args.change: Add a scheduler layer (cron-like) using Cloudflare Worker Cron Triggers and/or Durable Object alarms to run jobs later or on a cadence. Scheduling only triggers planning; execution happens on the appropriate surface (Mac or browser) with receipts and user-visible reminders when needed.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Enables “check every morning” and “remind me if this changes” without the owner having to ask repeatedly, and without keeping the Mac awake.
args.effort: High: needs new infrastructure, persistence, failure handling, and a user-facing way to define routines and quiet hours.

args.cost_impact: Ongoing compute/storage cost for scheduled triggers; dominated by downstream work. Still cheaper than constant polling from the relay.
args.latency_impact: Not latency-sensitive; work happens in the background. Relay only needs quick acknowledgments.
args.security_impact: Routines touch sensitive accounts; require clear scope per routine and store minimal tokens/credentials, ideally delegated to surfaces that already hold auth.
depends_on: Durable job ledger for tracking and receipts

args.user_asks: While you are carrying out something I asked from the pendant, let me say “stop,” “pause,” or “that’s enough,” and have the whole operation halt promptly across the Mac and any authenticated browser tab, then tell me exactly what did and did not happen.
args.why_useful: Today a spoken request can hand work to a downstream agent, but the owner may be away from the Mac and cannot safely interrupt an in-flight multi-step operation. A wearable-level abort is especially valuable for accidental commands, changed intent, or an unexpected side effect. This is genuinely hive-specific: the pendant hears the interruption, the always-awake relay identifies the active operation, and Mac/browser workers must cooperatively stop and report a consistent partial result.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles only the short interruption classification and spoken acknowledgement. A deterministic relay/job controller propagates cancellation; downstream agents use their existing models only to reach a safe action boundary and summarize the receipt.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the stop locally/in the relay within 300 ms where possible; send cancellation to all workers within 1 s; provide a final partial-operation receipt within 3 s. If a worker cannot stop immediately, say so explicitly rather than claiming success.
args.cost_estimate: Usually one short realtime turn (roughly $0.01–$0.05 depending on audio duration); cancellation and receipts are mostly control-plane work. No model call should be needed for the final status unless the partial result requires summarization.
args.security_concerns: The relay must bind an interruption to the owner’s active session/job and reject stale or guessed job IDs. Cancellation cannot undo an already-committed external mutation, so the spoken response must distinguish cancelled, completed, and unknown. Persist an immutable receipt of actions reached before the stop; do not transmit unrelated microphone audio or page contents.

One aggregated receipt schema that merges Mac and browser partial results and can be spoken concisely
Idempotent cancel handling so repeated “stop” commands are harmless

args.user_asks: If the Mac drops offline while you are doing something for me, keep the task going in the server browser where that is possible; if the browser cannot reach the needed session, pause and resume on my Mac when it returns, without making me repeat the request.
args.why_useful: The owner wears the pendant away from the Mac, so connectivity and substrate availability change during real tasks. Today work is tied to whichever downstream surface received it. args.model_tier: Realtime only acknowledges the handoff and reports status. A cheaper background controller serializes and migrates the task; the planner/model is invoked only to re-plan steps that differ between substrates.
args.latency_budget: Detect a lost worker within 5 s, announce that the task is being preserved within 1 s of the next pendant interaction, and resume on an eligible surface within 10 s of availability. Never silently replay a mutation after migration.
args.cost_estimate: Control-plane persistence is negligible; a migrated task generally costs one planner call (roughly $0.02–$0.15 depending on plan size) plus any browser/Mac execution calls. Keeping a compact action graph rather than transcript context limits repeated-token cost.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated browser cookies and Mac-local data must never be copied between substrates. Each step declares required capabilities and data locality; only portable inputs and redacted state cross the relay. Mutating steps need idempotency keys and must be marked committed/unknown before a retry. The owner hears which surface acted and which steps were skipped.

Checkpoint serialization of planner state, browser tab identity, Mac action receipts, and committed/unknown outcomes
A worker lease/heartbeat protocol and deterministic failover controller
Idempotency keys plus recovery rules preventing duplicate external mutations
A capability-aware migration planner that can substitute server-browser, Mac, or browser-extension steps without exporting secrets
Owner-visible spoken status for paused, migrated, resumed, and permanently blocked tasks

args.user_asks: When a task is running, let me long-press the pendant’s single button to abort it silently, even if speech recognition is unavailable, and flash the LED to show whether the abort was accepted, pending uplink, or too late to prevent a committed action.
args.why_useful: A wearable control must remain usable in traffic, a meeting, loud environments, or when the owner cannot safely speak.
