transcript.text:
Recorded three new capabilities:

1. **Private meeting capture** — start/stop from the pendant, produce action items, and draft follow-ups using calendar, Mac, and browser context.
2. **Cross-surface contract/invoice verification** — compare local contracts with authenticated browser invoices and report cited discrepancies.
3. **Voice-triggered outage triage** — correlate Mac logs, Git state, and authenticated deployment dashboards, then provide a read-only diagnosis and safest next step.

What is still needed:

- A durable background worker for transcription, document comparison, and incident analysis.
- Cross-surface evidence joining with source citations and timestamp normalization.
- Local redaction of secrets before relay/model submission.
- Pendant audio capture with explicit physical recording feedback and encrypted buffering.
- Browser-to-Mac evidence exchange while preserving browser session privacy.
- A voice-sized result channel for long-running jobs, including progress and completion summaries.
I’ll quickly scan what’s available now, then I’ll propose a few high-impact capabilities and call out any missing pieces.

result.name: relay_job_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). args.why_useful: A daily change brief that joins authenticated browser state with local project activity would replace manually reopening tabs and hunting through diffs. The important novelty is evidence-linked conversational comparison: the owner can challenge a claim from the pendant and receive the underlying tab/file source rather than an opaque summary.
args.model_tier: A cheaper background model computes incremental summaries and indexes citations; realtime only answers the owner’s follow-up question and routes any requested inspection to the correct surface.
args.latency_budget: Precompute in under two minutes after the chosen baseline; first spoken answer under 2 seconds, with cited detail fetched asynchronously if needed.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.02–$0.10 per daily brief, dominated by changed-page/file extraction; hash-based unchanged-content skipping keeps it low.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated browser pages and source code must remain scoped to explicitly selected tabs/projects. Store hashes and redacted excerpts where possible, keep full evidence local to the Mac/browser, and require an explicit selection before adding a new source.
missing: A baseline-and-diff store spanning browser pages and local project files
Stable evidence IDs that can be opened back on the originating Mac/browser surface
A citation-aware summarizer and voice follow-up retrieval path
A user-visible source-selection and retention control

args.change: Add a tiny coin vibration motor with a dedicated low-side driver to the pendant, and expose three firmware patterns (single short pulse, double pulse, escalating pulse) to the relay. Keep the existing LED as a visual channel but make haptics independently controllable for spoken capture, task handoff, and completion/error events.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can reliably know that the wearable heard them, started recording, or finished work without looking at it—especially outdoors, in a pocket, or in a noisy meeting where an LED and audio prompt are useless. It makes asynchronous Mac/browser work trustworthy while preserving silent operation.
args.effort: Moderate hardware revision and enclosure change; firmware event API plus relay mappings and battery characterization. Prototype can be tested on the USB-connected pendant with an external driver before a board spin.
args.risk: Added vibration can be distracting and may drain the small battery; provide intensity limits, a silent mode, and a physical long-press override. If the motor driver fails, all existing LED/audio behavior remains usable.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $1–$3 in parts at prototype quantities, plus a few mA only during pulses; negligible API cost because patterns are event metadata rather than model output.
args.latency_impact: Local acknowledgement can be under 100 ms; remote event patterns follow existing link latency and should not delay voice responses.
args.security_impact: No new data leaves the device. Firmware must reject arbitrary high-duty-cycle patterns so a compromised relay cannot silently exhaust the battery or annoy the owner.
depends_on: A small pendant firmware event channel for acknowledgement/completion states
Relay-side mapping of operation outcomes to haptic patterns
Battery and enclosure validation on the live nRF9160 pendant

args.user_asks: “Draft the reply from the page and files I’m looking at, then tell me exactly which private facts and attachments would leave my devices before I send it.”
args.why_useful: The owner can currently ask an agent to act across Mac and authenticated browser surfaces, but cannot get a trustworthy, human-readable account of the assembled outbound payload. This capability turns the pendant into a data-boundary assistant: it gathers only explicitly referenced material, identifies secrets and personal data, and produces a spoken diff before any send action.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model to assemble and classify the draft and payload; realtime only narrates the short risk summary and handles corrections. Sending remains an explicit downstream action after the owner hears the preview, without adding a blanket policy gate to unrelated actions.
args.latency_budget: Read the first concise preview within 3 seconds; full attachment and sensitive-span analysis may continue for up to 15 seconds with progress surfaced to the pendant.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.03–$0.15 per composed message, dominated by extracting referenced page/file contents and classification; hashes and cached local scans reduce repeat cost.
args.security_concerns: The analyzer itself sees exactly the sensitive material it is protecting. Keep raw files on the Mac whenever possible, send only spans/hashes to the relay, redact credentials and tokens in logs, show destination/account/attachments in the spoken and dashboard preview, and retain no draft after completion unless requested.
missing: A cross-surface outbound-payload builder with explicit source selection
Local secret/PII classification and redaction that returns spans rather than uploading full files
A typed preview receipt that downstream send actions must reference
A pendant-friendly spoken diff for destination, recipients, attachments, and sensitive fields

result.name: relay_job_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). Reads the relay job records; needs no Mac round trip, so it answers with the Mac asleep. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: reading live device state such as battery/wifi/volume/frontmost app (get_mac_status), or starting new work (mac_run_actions / mac_delegate). Speak the returned `spoken` sentence essentially verbatim; it already names the task and is sized for the pendant speaker. NEVER upgrade its wording — if it says failed, queued, or unknown, say that; do not report a task as done that this tool did not call done.

reference.description: How the owner referred to the task, in their own words ("that", "the Outlook thing", "what I asked earlier"). Pass it through verbatim; do not invent detail. Omit only if they gave none.

job_id.description: Only when the owner named an exact relay job id. Normally omitted.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

args.change: Add a pendant-side transaction control channel over the live USB serial link: a short button press emits cancel-current-job, a double press emits repeat-last-status, and a long press emits emergency-stop; the relay maps these to the active Mac/browser job by correlation id and returns a distinct LED pattern for acknowledged, cancelled, and link-lost states. args.risk: A false press could cancel useful work; require a long press for emergency-stop and make cancellation idempotent. If serial framing breaks, fall back to current voice behavior and show link-lost LED; never infer success without relay acknowledgement.
args.cost_impact: No API cost; negligible firmware CPU/RAM and under 1 mA transient LED/button activity. Engineering cost is the serial protocol and tests.
args.latency_impact: Local button acknowledgement under 100 ms; relay action bounded by existing job cancellation/status latency.
args.security_impact: The physical pendant becomes an authenticated control surface. Bind events to the paired device/session and reject stale correlation ids; emergency-stop should not expose task contents over serial.

transcript.text:
Recorded four proposals:

1. **Human handoff bridge:** dictate a situation, draft/send it through Messages, Mail, or an authenticated browser session, then have replies spoken back through the pendant.
2. **Self-healing task execution:** detect failures, stale tabs, timeouts, or disconnects; retry safe operations once through an alternate route and provide a concise spoken receipt.
3. **Private end-of-day debrief:** combine voice history, Mac receipts, and browser results into a short spoken summary of unresolved commitments, with “snooze” and “close” follow-ups.
4. **Physical pendant transaction controls:** use button presses to cancel the active job, repeat status, or emergency-stop, with LED acknowledgement over the currently connected USB hardware.

The main missing pieces are cross-surface correlation and event delivery, durable conversation/debrief state, Mac/browser message adapters, idempotent retry policy, and firmware support for acknowledged button events.
I’m going to quickly inventory what’s available now, then I’ll propose a few high-impact capabilities and call out gaps to fill.

result.name: relay_job_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). Reads the relay job records; needs no Mac round trip, so it answers with the Mac asleep. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: reading live device state such as battery/wifi/volume/frontmost app (get_mac_status), or starting new work (mac_run_actions / mac_delegate). Speak the returned `spoken` sentence essentially verbatim; it already names the task and is sized for the pendant speaker. NEVER upgrade its wording — if it says failed, queued, or unknown, say that; do not report a task as done that this tool did not call done.

reference.description: How the owner referred to the task, in their own words ("that", "the Outlook thing", "what I asked earlier"). Pass it through verbatim; do not invent detail. Omit only if they gave none.

job_id.description: Only when the owner named an exact relay job id. Normally omitted.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

args.user_asks: Use my pendant as a physical “handoff” button: when I press it near my Mac, make the relay identify my active work context and send a compact, private handoff to the Mac or browser session I choose, without me dictating it.

result.name: relay_job_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). Reads the relay job records; needs no Mac round trip, so it answers with the Mac asleep. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: reading live device state such as battery/wifi/volume/frontmost app (get_mac_status), or starting new work (mac_run_actions / mac_delegate). Speak the returned `spoken` sentence essentially verbatim; it already names the task and is sized for the pendant speaker. NEVER upgrade its wording — if it says failed, queued, or unknown, say that; do not report a task as done that this tool did not call done.

reference.description: How the owner referred to the task, in their own words ("that", "the Outlook thing", "what I asked earlier"). Pass it through verbatim; do not invent detail. Omit only if they gave none.

job_id.description: Only when the owner named an exact relay job id. Normally omitted.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.name: relay_route_intent
result.why: As a low-latency front door, I need a safe, explicit way to route recognized user intents to downstream agents (mac-planner/mac-vision) and receive status, without inventing my own protocol.
result.status: Granted as a schema. Calling it returns a note saying it has no implementation yet — describe what you would do with it rather than assuming it acts.

result.name: mac_run_actions
result.description: PROACTIVE for reversible control. Execute 1–3 concrete Mac actions when the Mac surface is online: open_app, open_url, open_path, create_reminder, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, run_shell (allowlisted system intents), run_applescript, and similar. Prefer high-level types over raw shell when a typed action exists. Use when: owner wants to change or run something on the Mac that is not a pure status read. Do NOT use when: only reading battery/wifi/volume/focused app (get_mac_status), browser page work (browser_run_actions), public facts (web_search), or long multi-step ambiguous workflows (mac_delegate). Confirmation first only for destructive actions. Never claim success without this tool (or get_mac_status) actually queuing work.

actions.description: 1–3 concrete actions for the Mac executor (primary product of this tool).

type.description: Executor action type. Examples: run_shell, run_applescript, create_reminder, open_app, open_url, open_path, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, browser_snapshot, browser_list_tabs, browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_wait_for, browser_read_page, browser_select.

label.description: Short human-readable label for logs / UI.

params.description: Parameters for the action type. Use only fields that type needs (e.g. command for run_shell, title/due for create_reminder, url for open_url or browser_navigate, selector/text for browser_click/type, appName for open_app matching the Mac software inventory exactly).

spoken_reply.description: Short confirmation for the pendant speaker (preferred user-facing reply).

transcript.description: Optional short transcript for history/debug only. Omit if unsure — never block on this; plan from audio via actions.

result.button: ONE user button, devicetree alias sw0. Press starts a conversation; second press ends it. It is also pokable over J-Link for testing.
result.led: ONE LED, alias led0. Currently signals recording, stays solid while agent audio is buffered, and flashes error codes.
result.buses: GPIO, I2C, SPI and I2S all enabled (prj.conf). I2C and SPI are FREE — nothing is attached to them today.
result.caution: There is exactly one I2S peripheral and it runs full duplex (mic in + speaker out) with byte-identical TX/RX config. Any new audio path must share it.
result.status: PROTOTYPE. This is a Nordic development kit, not the product. Every choice here — the SoC, the RAM, the single button, the single LED, the enclosure — is provisional and can change. Design the device the owner should wear, then say what it would take to build it.
result.you_are_here: You run on a Cloudflare Worker. The pendant and ESP32 below are REMOTE devices you talk to over the network; you are not running on them.

args.why_useful: It turns the relay into a reliable voice status desk. The owner can ask from anywhere and get an accurate update without waking the Mac.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the spoken response; no heavy planning.
args.latency_budget: Under a second if the relay has the job record; otherwise it should say it cannot find a record and suggest what to ask for next.
args.cost_estimate: Very low. One relay job-status lookup dominates; no Mac round trip.
args.security_concerns: Job summaries may include sensitive task names. Only read the owner’s own job records and speak the returned sentence verbatim to avoid accidental reinterpretation.

args.user_asks: “When I press the pendant button, tell me whether I am actually near my Mac, and only then carry out the desktop task I just spoke; if I am away, queue it for when I return and tell me which mode you chose.”
args.why_useful: The owner currently cannot make the worn pendant adapt safely to physical presence. This joins a real USB-connected pendant, Mac presence evidence, relay conversation, and downstream Mac/browser action into one behavior: immediate execution when home, durable intent handoff when away, with an audible explanation rather than a silent failure.
args.model_tier: Realtime relay for the short spoken decision; a cheaper background classifier on the Mac/relay for presence evidence and intent normalization; gpt-5.6-luna only when the queued task needs planning.
args.latency_budget: Button acknowledgement under 300 ms; presence verdict under 2 s; task execution may be asynchronous and must produce a later spoken or LED result.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per interaction depending on whether planning is needed; dominant cost is the realtime turn, not presence checks.
args.security_concerns: USB serial presence and microphone-derived proximity signals leave the device/relay only as coarse state, never raw audio. A false 'home' verdict could run a desktop mutation, so the system must be explicit about uncertainty and default to queueing rather than pretending the Mac is reachable.
missing: A relay endpoint that receives pendant button/audio state and correlates it with the Mac's live heartbeat
A signed, short-lived proximity proof between /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* pendant and the Mac
A durable intent queue with reconnect delivery and spoken/LED completion notices
A presence-aware routing policy distinct from the existing action receipts

args.user_asks: “Before you act, notice when the Mac, browser, and my remembered preferences disagree; ask me one concise question on the pendant, then use my answer as the authoritative correction everywhere.”
args.why_useful: Today the owner can receive a confident but wrong result when surfaces disagree (for example, timezone or browser frame access). A spoken contradiction-resolution loop would turn hidden cross-agent inconsistencies into a single answer the owner can correct, instead of forcing them to inspect logs or repeat themselves.
args.model_tier: Cheap background perception compares typed evidence and detects contradictions; realtime is reserved for the one clarification question and confirmation; no expensive planning unless the corrected fact changes the task.
args.latency_budget: Detect during normal task completion; ask within 1 s of detecting a material contradiction; resume after one answer within 3 s.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.001–$0.005 per task when a contradiction exists; most tasks use only local comparison and cost nothing beyond the normal turn.
args.security_concerns: The system must distinguish observed facts from owner assertions and retain provenance. Never silently overwrite a secret or account setting; store the correction as a scoped, versioned preference and announce what scope changed.
missing: A typed evidence/provenance envelope shared by relay, Mac, browser, and faculty agents
A durable owner-correction store with scope and expiry (session, device, or global)
A low-latency spoken clarification/answer exchange that can interrupt a pending downstream job
A contradiction severity policy so harmless differences do not annoy the owner

args.user_asks: “Learn my voice once, then ignore commands spoken by other people near the pendant; if you are unsure, ask me to press the button and repeat instead of sending anything to my Mac.”
args.why_useful: A worn microphone is exposed to coworkers, family, and media. Today any captured speech can become a trusted command. Voice identity plus a physical-button fallback gives the owner a practical boundary between conversation and control without requiring the Mac to be nearby.
args.model_tier: Local DSP/embedding on the ESP32 or pendant for the first filter; realtime only handles accepted speech; a background model manages enrollment quality and drift.

transcript.text: I’m going to pull a couple of concrete specs so the proposals are grounded in what’s actually present, then I’ll lay out the new capabilities and gaps.

result.name: relay_route_intent
result.why: As a low-latency front door, I need a safe, explicit way to route recognized user intents to downstream agents (mac-planner/mac-vision) and receive status, without inventing my own protocol.
result.status: Granted as a schema. Calling it returns a note saying it has no implementation yet — describe what you would do with it rather than assuming it acts.

result.name: server_browser_actions
result.why: Enable the relay to run safe, sandboxed browser interactions without relying on the owner’s Mac being online, using Cloudflare Browser Run when available.
result.status: Granted as a schema. Calling it returns a note saying it has no implementation yet — describe what you would do with it rather than assuming it acts.

result.name: relay_job_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). Reads the relay job records; needs no Mac round trip, so it answers with the Mac asleep. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: reading live device state such as battery/wifi/volume/frontmost app (get_mac_status), or starting new work (mac_run_actions / mac_delegate). Speak the returned `spoken` sentence essentially verbatim; it already names the task and is sized for the pendant speaker. NEVER upgrade its wording — if it says failed, queued, or unknown, say that; do not report a task as done that this tool did not call done.

reference.description: How the owner referred to the task, in their own words ("that", "the Outlook thing", "what I asked earlier"). Pass it through verbatim; do not invent detail. Omit only if they gave none.

job_id.description: Only when the owner named an exact relay job id. Normally omitted.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.mic: I2S microphone, 15,625 Hz capture, Opus-encoded uplink at 16 kHz / 16 kbps, complexity 0
result.playback: Opus decode on-device at 24 kHz / 60 ms frames, resampled to the 31,250 Hz I2S wire clock, out to the ESP32 bridge
result.codec: libopus 1.6.1 vendored, fixed-point, built -O3. Decode ~25.4 ms per 60 ms packet; encode ~15.0 ms per call. Roughly 87% of one core when both run.
result.status: PROTOTYPE. This is a Nordic development kit, not the product. Every choice here — the SoC, the RAM, the single button, the single LED, the enclosure — is provisional and can change. Design the device the owner should wear, then say what it would take to build it.
result.you_are_here: You run on a Cloudflare Worker. The pendant and ESP32 below are REMOTE devices you talk to over the network; you are not running on them.

result.link: LTE-M (Cat-M1) via the nRF9160 modem. Half duplex in practice.
result.transport: One TLS WebSocket to the Cloudflare Worker carries uplink and downlink audio simultaneously. Modem TLS record limit is about 2 kB.
result.measured: Uplink 16 kbps + downlink 24 kbps saturates the link under contention: a recent call dropped 388 uplink packets (~7.8 s of speech) when the agent was speaking at the same time the owner was.

transcript.text: I’m going to propose three concrete capabilities and the changes they’d require, then I’ll summarize the key missing pieces I still need.

args.user_asks: If this takes a while, keep going after I stop talking and tell me exactly what happened when it’s done.
args.why_useful: This is the single most useful behavior for a wearable assistant: the owner can delegate a multi-step task and walk away, then get a clear completion report later without babysitting it.
args.model_tier: Realtime for intake and confirmation; cheaper planner/model for the long-running work and summarization.
args.latency_budget: Intake under a second; work may run minutes. Status updates should be near-instant when asked, even if the Mac is asleep.
args.cost_estimate: Low per spoken request at the relay; bulk cost is downstream planning/execution and any page reads. Avoid re-sending large context; store job metadata once.
args.security_concerns: Actions taken on the owner’s behalf must be reversible where possible and reported with receipts. No silent submission of forms. Only the minimal necessary data leaves devices and it should be logged with provenance.
missing: A durable job runner for relay-originated tasks (not just Mac-local execution)
Reliable status/receipt retrieval from the relay surface
A completion-summary queue the pendant can pick up later
A signed device-presence event stream so the relay knows when the pendant can receive updates

result.why: This restates something the system already has, so it was not recorded.
result.alreadyHave: Keep working after I stop talking, then tell me what happened when it’s done. The owner can start a task on the go, walk away, and still get a clear outcome later without babysitting the Mac or browser.
result.next: Propose something this does not already cover, or say what it should become that it is not today.

args.user_asks: Run a quick audio health check and tell me if my mic, bridge, and network are behaving before I start a call.
args.why_useful: When the owner is about to ask for help, a fast “your setup is good” reduces friction and prevents a bad experience from packet loss or miswired audio.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the spoken result; diagnostics and analysis should be automated and cheap.
args.latency_budget: A few seconds. It should be short enough to run right before a conversation.
args.cost_estimate: Cheap: a brief tone/loopback and a small diagnostic report. Biggest cost is any cross-surface coordination and logging.
args.security_concerns: No sensitive content is needed; use synthetic audio. Log only counters and timestamps. Avoid storing the test audio unless the owner asks.
missing: A device skill to generate and loop back a test signal on the pendant/bridge
Cross-surface USB presence detection and truthful counters (packet loss, jitter, buffer underruns)
A relay-visible event/report channel for diagnostics results

args.change: Implement relay_route_intent as the explicit routing front door with job tracking. The relay should accept a routed intent, create a durable job record, forward to the right downstream surface (Mac planner or browser harness), and store minimal context for status and receipts.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Voice commands become reliable and traceable. The owner can ask what happened later and get an exact answer, even if the Mac slept.
args.effort: Medium to high. Requires a job table, intent schema versioning, and downstream forwarding with retries.
args.risk: Misrouting could trigger wrong actions. Mitigate with receipts, clear spoken confirmations for irreversible actions, and idempotency keys.
args.cost_impact: Moderate engineering time; runtime cost is small per request if context is minimized.
args.latency_impact: Intake stays fast; long work runs elsewhere. Adds negligible overhead to routing.
args.security_impact: Creates a new control plane. Needs auth, auditing, and strict logging of what was sent where.
depends_on: Durable job storage and receipts on the relay
Downstream endpoint for routed intents (Mac planner and browser harness)

Add a status callback path so downstream agents can update the relay job record and a spoken summary.

args.change: Add a cross-surface device presence and custody channel: signed pendant/bridge presence events from the Mac when USB is attached, plus relay-visible TTL capsules for tasks that require the device to be present.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Tasks that need the pendant (audio tests, playback, button interactions) won’t fail mysteriously; they run only when the device is actually available.
args.effort: Medium. Requires signing, event propagation, and TTL handling.
args.risk: If presence lies, the system will misbehave. Use signatures and short expiries; fall back to asking the owner to reconnect.
args.cost_impact: Low runtime overhead; some engineering across Mac and relay.
args.latency_impact: Small; presence checks should be cached and quick.
args.security_impact: Presence becomes a control signal; must be authenticated and tamper-resistant.
depends_on: Mac-side presence daemon and serial detection

args.user_asks: “When I press and hold the pendant button in an emergency, quietly let my trusted contact know where I am, keep a live check-in open, and tell me whether help acknowledged.”
args.why_useful: A worn, one-button device is the only surface available when the owner cannot reach a phone or Mac. It turns the pendant into a dependable safety lifeline rather than merely a voice remote.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles the immediate spoken acknowledgement and intent; a cheap background worker maintains retries and acknowledgement state. The Mac/browser performs the authenticated messaging or calling workflow when available.
args.latency_budget: Local button acknowledgement under 300 ms; first outbound notification under 10 s; retry and acknowledgement tracking may continue for minutes.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per incident in model/relay work, dominated by any SMS/voice provider and cellular data.
args.security_concerns: Requires explicit enrollment of trusted contacts, signed device events, anti-replay sequence numbers, and encrypted location. Location and emergency text leave the device; a long press must be deliberate and a visible dashboard audit trail should exist. Never expose contact data to the model beyond the selected policy.
missing: LTE-registered pendant event uplink and authenticated button-event endpoint
GNSS/location acquisition and encrypted location storage
durable retry/alarm worker with provider adapters
trusted-contact enrollment and acknowledgement callbacks
Mac/browser workflow for sending the notification when relay-only delivery is unavailable

args.user_asks: “While I am walking, keep a private rolling audio transcript of the last 90 seconds; when I say ‘save that’, bookmark the moment, summarize the useful idea later on my Mac, and let me retrieve it by asking the pendant.”
args.why_useful: Ideas and instructions disappear before the owner can reach a keyboard. A short rolling buffer gives them reliable recall without permanently recording everything, and combines the worn microphone, always-awake relay, and Mac for cheap delayed organization.
args.model_tier: Realtime only detects the save command and confirms it. An inexpensive background model transcribes and summarizes bookmarked segments on the Mac; the relay stores compact indexed metadata for later voice retrieval.
args.latency_budget: Save confirmation under 1 s; transcription within 30 s of bookmark; voice retrieval under 3 s for indexed notes.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.10 per saved clip depending on audio duration and transcription model; storage is small, with audio retention configurable.
args.security_concerns: The rolling audio must be encrypted and automatically discarded unless bookmarked. The pendant needs a conspicuous LED pattern and spoken confirmation; dashboard must show retention and deletion controls. Nearby voices may be captured, so owner-configured recording mode and local-only default are required.
missing: On-device or bridge rolling PCM/Opus ring buffer with bookmark event
Authenticated relay clip upload and encrypted object storage
Background transcription/indexing job and semantic retrieval endpoint
Pendant playback/query response path and deletion controls

args.user_asks: “When I arrive at my studio, prepare the exact work context I was using before I left—reopen the right Mac apps and browser tabs, restore drafts, and tell me what changed while I was away.”
args.why_useful: The owner loses time reconstructing context after travel or interruption. The pendant provides physical arrival and identity continuity, the relay coordinates state, and the Mac/browser can restore authenticated work without requiring a spoken multi-step command.
args.model_tier: A background, low-cost classifier compares signed departure/arrival capsules and produces a restore plan. Realtime is used only for a short arrival confirmation or correction; Mac planner executes the reversible restore and browser extension restores session-bound tabs.
args.latency_budget: Detect arrival within 15 s; owner hears a concise ready/status response within 5 s after confirmation; restoration completes within 60 s.
args.cost_estimate: Under $0.02 per arrival, dominated by a small state-diff model; no recurring model cost while idle. Browser and Mac API calls dominate execution time.
args.security_concerns: Arrival geofences and work context are sensitive. Store coarse location hashes, not raw tracks, and sign departure/arrival events. Restoring tabs may expose private pages to anyone near the Mac, so require the pendant's authenticated proximity proof and provide an immediate lock/undo action.
missing: Reliable pendant proximity/geofence events (GNSS or local beacon)
Durable context capsules capturing Mac windows, browser tabs, drafts, and departure timestamp

Arrival-triggered job scheduler and reversible Mac restore actions
Proximity proof stronger than bearer session identity

args.user_asks: “Translate this conversation for me in real time: whisper the other person’s speech in my ear, and speak my replies in their language when I press the button.”
args.why_useful: The pendant and audio bridge can mediate a face-to-face conversation without the owner holding a phone or looking at a screen. The Mac can supply a richer language model when nearby, while the relay keeps the interaction usable when it is not.
args.model_tier: Realtime speech detection, translation, and short utterance generation use the low-latency tier; a cheaper background model maintains a per-conversation glossary and language detection. The Mac is an optional high-quality fallback, not a requirement.
args.latency_budget: Detect speech and start translated playback within 1.5 s for short utterances; button-to-spoken reply under 2 s; degrade to buffered translation rather than fabricate when confidence is low.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.05–$0.30 per minute of active translated speech, dominated by streaming transcription and synthesis; idle cost is zero.
args.security_concerns: Conversation audio leaves the pendant and may include bystanders. Require an explicit start/stop gesture, a visible recording LED, encrypted transport, configurable no-retention mode, and no transcript persistence by default. The owner should be able to cancel playback instantly.
missing: Full-duplex low-latency audio transport between ESP32 bridge, relay, and pendant
Streaming ASR/translation/TTS with interruption and echo cancellation

transcript.text:
Recorded four capabilities. The most important missing pieces are:

- **Authenticated pendant event uplink** for button presses, proximity, and location.
- **Durable background jobs and retries** for emergency escalation, transcription, and arrival workflows.
- **Encrypted short-lived audio buffering** with explicit recording indicators and deletion.
- **Full-duplex low-latency audio** between ESP32, relay, and pendant, including streaming ASR, translation, TTS, interruption, and echo cancellation.
- **Cross-surface state capsules** that capture Mac/browser context and restore it only after authenticated pendant proximity.
- **Trusted-contact enrollment, acknowledgement callbacks, and emergency provider integration.**
- **Privacy controls** for location, audio retention, browser-session restoration, and proximity authentication.

The existing routes mostly provide ingredients; the owner still cannot use these capabilities because the durable event, audio, identity, and cross-surface orchestration layers between them do not exist.
I’m going to quickly inventory what’s available now, then I’ll highlight the most useful next capabilities and what’s still missing.

args.user_asks: “When I say ‘make this safe,’ use the pendant as my physical presence signal: immediately mute Mac microphones, pause recording/streaming apps, hide or lock authenticated browser tabs, and tell me what was changed; when I return and press the button, restore only the state you recorded.”
args.why_useful: A worn, always-available control is the one surface that can react when the owner notices a privacy risk, even away from the Mac. It turns the pendant into a practical emergency privacy switch rather than another voice remote.

args.security_concerns: The pendant credential becomes a physical privacy token, so replay protection, device sequence numbers, and an append-only before/after receipt are required. Reads the relay job records; needs no Mac round trip, so it answers with the Mac asleep. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: reading live device state such as battery/wifi/volume/frontmost app (get_mac_status), or starting new work (mac_run_actions / mac_delegate). Speak the returned `spoken` sentence essentially verbatim; it already names the task and is sized for the pendant speaker. NEVER upgrade its wording — if it says failed, queued, or unknown, say that; do not report a task as done that this tool did not call done.

reference.description: How the owner referred to the task, in their own words ("that", "the Outlook thing", "what I asked earlier"). Pass it through verbatim; do not invent detail. Omit only if they gave none.

job_id.description: Only when the owner named an exact relay job id. Normally omitted.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.name: mac_delegate
result.description: ONLY for multi-step or ambiguous computer tasks that cannot fit a short action list. Hands the goal to the local Mac agent (sets requireLocalPlanner). Use when: complex multi-app workflows, unclear steps, long-running computer use. Do NOT use when: a single get_mac_status or 1–3 mac_run_actions / browser_run_actions would suffice. Prefer concrete tools first.

goal.description: Clear goal for the Mac agent to accomplish.

spoken_reply.description: Optional short confirmation for the pendant speaker while the Mac works.

transcript.description: Optional short transcript for history/debug only. Omit if unsure.

result.name: mac_run_actions
result.description: PROACTIVE for reversible control. Execute 1–3 concrete Mac actions when the Mac surface is online: open_app, open_url, open_path, create_reminder, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, run_shell (allowlisted system intents), run_applescript, and similar. Prefer high-level types over raw shell when a typed action exists. Use when: owner wants to change or run something on the Mac that is not a pure status read. Do NOT use when: only reading battery/wifi/volume/focused app (get_mac_status), browser page work (browser_run_actions), public facts (web_search), or long multi-step ambiguous workflows (mac_delegate). Confirmation first only for destructive actions. Never claim success without this tool (or get_mac_status) actually queuing work.

actions.description: 1–3 concrete actions for the Mac executor (primary product of this tool).

type.description: Executor action type. Examples: run_shell, run_applescript, create_reminder, open_app, open_url, open_path, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, browser_snapshot, browser_list_tabs, browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_wait_for, browser_read_page, browser_select.

label.description: Short human-readable label for logs / UI.

params.description: Parameters for the action type. Use only fields that type needs (e.g. command for run_shell, title/due for create_reminder, url for open_url or browser_navigate, selector/text for browser_click/type, appName for open_app matching the Mac software inventory exactly).

spoken_reply.description: Short confirmation for the pendant speaker (preferred user-facing reply).

transcript.description: Optional short transcript for history/debug only. Omit if unsure — never block on this; plan from audio via actions.

transcript.text: I’m going to outline a few high-impact things this system should be able to do, and flag what’s missing to make them real.

args.user_asks: Keep listening and keep the thread going across my devices—if I stop talking on the pendant, pick back up on the Mac or browser without losing context.
args.why_useful: This would feel like a single conversation that follows the owner, instead of a bunch of disconnected sessions. It’s the most useful thing because it removes the biggest friction: context loss when switching surfaces.
args.model_tier: Realtime for turn-by-turn speech; cheaper planner models for continuation and tool use when the owner isn’t actively speaking.
args.latency_budget: Sub-second while the owner is speaking; seconds are fine when resuming on another surface.
args.cost_estimate: Low for voice turns; higher when summarizing long context or querying sessions. Cost dominated by context transfer and session reconciliation.
args.security_concerns: Conversation history is sensitive. Only the owner’s surfaces should be able to resume. Needs explicit session binding and audit logs.
missing: A relay-visible session inventory endpoint so the relay can see its own conversations
A durable conversation state store keyed to the owner and session
A reliable event channel to notify the Mac/browser to resume

Never claim legitimacy from one source, and clearly say when evidence is unavailable. Require explicit confirmation before sending, paying, deleting, or replying.

transcript.text:
Recorded four new capabilities. The owner still needs:

1. **Cross-device legitimacy checks**  
   The pendant should investigate a message, invoice, offer, or webpage across authenticated browser sessions and Mac data, then return a cited verdict with uncertainty and conflicting evidence.

2. **Marked-moment memory**  
   A button press plus “save this moment” should preserve a bounded audio segment and correlate it with the active Mac window, calendar event, browser tab, and follow-up context for later spoken retrieval.

3. **Semantic change digest**  
   The owner should be able to ask “what changed since I left?” and receive only important changes across the Mac, browser, and relay jobs, with the ability to select an item verbally for action.

4. **Context-aware clarification**  
   When a request could refer to multiple visible documents or tabs, the relay should inspect active Mac/browser context and ask one precise clarification rather than guessing.

The main missing pieces are not individual actions; they are cross-surface coordination:

- bounded, locally indicated audio capture and retention;
- timestamped context correlation across pendant, Mac, and browser;
- semantic evidence/diff indexes with citations and expiration;
- conversational state that pauses an intent, asks one clarification, and resumes safely;
- asynchronous result delivery back to the pendant;
- provenance-rich receipts tying each answer or action to its sources.

The first capability—evidence-backed legitimacy checking—is the most valuable: it combines the wearable’s immediate access, the browser’s authenticated sessions, and the Mac’s private local context into something no single surface can provide today.
I’m going to quickly inventory what’s available, then I’ll propose a few high-impact capabilities and call out what’s still missing.

result.name: relay_job_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). Reads the relay job records; needs no Mac round trip, so it answers with the Mac asleep. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: reading live device state such as battery/wifi/volume/frontmost app (get_mac_status), or starting new work (mac_run_actions / mac_delegate). Speak the returned `spoken` sentence essentially verbatim; it already names the task and is sized for the pendant speaker. NEVER upgrade its wording — if it says failed, queued, or unknown, say that; do not report a task as done that this tool did not call done.

reference.description: How the owner referred to the task, in their own words ("that", "the Outlook thing", "what I asked earlier"). Pass it through verbatim; do not invent detail. Omit only if they gave none.

job_id.description: Only when the owner named an exact relay job id. Normally omitted.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.description: PROACTIVE. transcript.text:
Recorded four new capabilities/changes:

1. **Exact-context voice inspection and action** across the active Mac screen and authenticated browser tab, with evidence-bound follow-up execution.
2. **Departure/return work continuity**: snapshot the active editor, terminal, and browser context when leaving, then report only meaningful changes and restore the exact location on return.
3. **Voice-driven bug repair loop**: investigate, reproduce across Mac/browser, patch, run tests, and report only verified results.
4. **Sensitive-content guardian** for screenshot, browser extraction, and spoken readback, with local redaction and explicit one-shot reveal.
5. **Pendant haptic/touch feedback** for private status, completion, redaction, and immediate local cancel/mute.

What is still needed is primarily the connective layer: stable cross-surface snapshot IDs, event delivery from the pendant, durable evidence/job bundles, streamed Mac test output, browser-to-terminal handoff, and local privacy classification before data reaches the relay.
I’m going to take a quick inventory of what’s available now, then I’ll propose a few high-impact capabilities and call out any missing pieces.

result.name: relay_job_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). Reads the relay job records; needs no Mac round trip, so it answers with the Mac asleep. Call immediately — no confirmation. args.user_asks: Use my pendant as a physical presence key: when I say “use my private browser,” only a currently-attached or recently authenticated pendant can authorize the relay to operate my authenticated browser tabs, and the pendant immediately tells me if that presence expires while work is running.
args.why_useful: It lets the owner safely delegate real authenticated work while away from the Mac without relying on a typed password or a vague cloud session. Stealing a browser cookie alone would not be enough; the worn object becomes the human-presence boundary.
args.model_tier: No expensive reasoning for authorization; use deterministic firmware/relay checks. Realtime speech is only for the owner’s command and concise expiry warning.
args.latency_budget: Presence verification under 200 ms over USB or under 2 seconds over LTE; browser commands should start within 3 seconds; expiry warning immediately on loss.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost; approximately $5–$20 for a secure-element-backed pendant revision, plus tiny relay storage and heartbeat traffic.
args.security_concerns: A compromised Mac, relay, or pendant could impersonate presence. Use challenge-response keys, nonce-bound job tokens, replay protection, short leases, revocation, and never speak secrets aloud. This is an authorization boundary, not a claim that the pendant proves identity at a distance.

A relay presence-lease service that binds each browser/Mac job to a nonce and expiry
Browser and Mac command handlers that reject jobs whose lease is absent or stale
A visible pendant LED pattern and dashboard audit trail for lease state

args.subject: Novel cross-node gaps proposed this round
args.body: I recorded four capabilities: physical-presence lease for authenticated browser use; independent Mac/browser effect prediction and disagreement report; pendant emergency-stop propagation with receipts; and voice bookmark correlated with Mac/browser state. transcript.text:
Recorded four capabilities:

1. **Voice bookmarks tied to digital context** — save a spoken note with the Mac’s active app and authenticated browser state, then retrieve it later with citations.
2. **Pendant-backed physical presence** — require a cryptographic pendant lease before operating authenticated browser sessions.
3. **Independent cross-node verification** — have Mac and browser agents predict effects independently, report disagreements, then execute with evidence and receipts.
4. **Pendant emergency stop** — double-press and say “stop” to cancel active Mac/browser workflows and hear exactly what completed versus what was prevented.

What remains needed is primarily new coordination and device support: durable cross-surface correlation, cryptographic pendant firmware, typed prediction/evidence schemas, cancellation checkpoints, and a relay path for spoken status outside an active conversation.
I’m going to quickly inventory what’s available now, then I’ll propose a few useful owner-facing capabilities and call out any missing pieces.

result.name: relay_job_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). Reads the relay job records; needs no Mac round trip, so it answers with the Mac asleep. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: reading live device state such as battery/wifi/volume/frontmost app (get_mac_status), or starting new work (mac_run_actions / mac_delegate). Speak the returned `spoken` sentence essentially verbatim; it already names the task and is sized for the pendant speaker. NEVER upgrade its wording — if it says failed, queued, or unknown, say that; do not report a task as done that this tool did not call done.

reference.description: How the owner referred to the task, in their own words ("that", "the Outlook thing", "what I asked earlier"). Pass it through verbatim; do not invent detail. Omit only if they gave none.

job_id.description: Only when the owner named an exact relay job id. Normally omitted.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

args.model_tier: Realtime model only classifies the short voice command; cancellation, checkpointing, and resume are deterministic worker behavior.

args.security_concerns: A false wake or speech recognition could interrupt work, so require the physical pendant button plus the spoken phrase for the global variant. Checkpoints must exclude secrets and never serialize browser credentials. Resume must be idempotent to avoid duplicate mutations.

args.model_tier: Realtime handles the short mode command; deterministic policy and notification state snapshots do the work. A cheap background model may rank deferred items when the mode ends.
args.latency_budget: Mute/suppress actions should begin within 1 second; the end-of-mode digest can arrive within 10 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero realtime inference for mode changes; optional small background ranking call per meeting. Main cost is platform integration and encrypted state storage.
args.security_concerns: The owner must be able to recover from a lost “meeting over” command. Persist a timeout and a visible dashboard override. Urgent rules must be explicit and local where possible; do not upload message contents merely to decide urgency.

relay policy engine, deferred-event queue, timeout, and spoken urgent interrupt

result.name: relay_job_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). Reads the relay job records; needs no Mac round trip, so it answers with the Mac asleep. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: reading live device state such as battery/wifi/volume/frontmost app (get_mac_status), or starting new work (mac_run_actions / mac_delegate). Speak the returned `spoken` sentence essentially verbatim; it already names the task and is sized for the pendant speaker. NEVER upgrade its wording — if it says failed, queued, or unknown, say that; do not report a task as done that this tool did not call done.

reference.description: How the owner referred to the task, in their own words ("that", "the Outlook thing", "what I asked earlier"). Pass it through verbatim; do not invent detail. Omit only if they gave none.

job_id.description: Only when the owner named an exact relay job id. Normally omitted.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.mic: I2S microphone, 15,625 Hz capture, Opus-encoded uplink at 16 kHz / 16 kbps, complexity 0
result.playback: Opus decode on-device at 24 kHz / 60 ms frames, resampled to the 31,250 Hz I2S wire clock, out to the ESP32 bridge
result.codec: libopus 1.6.1 vendored, fixed-point, built -O3. Decode ~25.4 ms per 60 ms packet; encode ~15.0 ms per call. Roughly 87% of one core when both run.

args.user_asks: “Check this before I send it.” Without changing anything, have the pendant inspect the focused draft on the Mac or browser, compare recipients, attachments, links, and claims against the surrounding document/context, and speak only concrete risks and a one-sentence suggested fix.

args.security_concerns: Drafts, recipients, and attachments are highly sensitive. Keep raw content on the Mac/extension where possible, send only hashes/extracted facts to the relay, encrypt any temporary payload, never auto-send or edit, and visibly state which surfaces were actually inspected.

args.why_useful: The owner can get a trustworthy engineering checkpoint while away from the keyboard instead of relying on a green-looking editor or memory. The Mac has the repository and test runtime; the relay and pendant make the result available during a walk; the report is grounded in executable evidence rather than a generic code opinion.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background planner for repository/test discovery and deterministic diff/test collection; reserve realtime for interpreting the collected evidence and speaking the compact result.
args.latency_budget: Start immediately, provide an audible 'testing started' acknowledgment within 500 ms, and deliver a first result within 30 seconds; long suites should return incremental completed/failed counts rather than blocking.
args.cost_estimate: Typically $0.03–$0.15 per review, dominated by test execution and a short synthesis; no screenshot cost unless the focused diff is only visible in a GUI.
args.security_concerns: Source code and test output may contain secrets or proprietary data. Keep execution on the Mac, redact credentials and unrelated files, include exact evidence paths and timestamps, and never merge, push, or mutate the repository without a separate explicit command.
missing: A Mac-terminal job endpoint that runs a bounded test plan and streams typed progress

result.name: mac_delegate
result.description: ONLY for multi-step or ambiguous computer tasks that cannot fit a short action list. Hands the goal to the local Mac agent (sets requireLocalPlanner). Use when: complex multi-app workflows, unclear steps, long-running computer use. Do NOT use when: a single get_mac_status or 1–3 mac_run_actions / browser_run_actions would suffice. Prefer concrete tools first.

goal.description: Clear goal for the Mac agent to accomplish.

spoken_reply.description: Optional short confirmation for the pendant speaker while the Mac works.

transcript.description: Optional short transcript for history/debug only. Omit if unsure.

result.name: relay_job_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). Reads the relay job records; needs no Mac round trip, so it answers with the Mac asleep. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: reading live device state such as battery/wifi/volume/frontmost app (get_mac_status), or starting new work (mac_run_actions / mac_delegate). Speak the returned `spoken` sentence essentially verbatim; it already names the task and is sized for the pendant speaker. NEVER upgrade its wording — if it says failed, queued, or unknown, say that; do not report a task as done that this tool did not call done.

reference.description: How the owner referred to the task, in their own words ("that", "the Outlook thing", "what I asked earlier"). Pass it through verbatim; do not invent detail. Omit only if they gave none.

job_id.description: Only when the owner named an exact relay job id. Normally omitted.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.board: Nordic nRF9160 DK (nRF9160 SiP), non-secure app under TF-M minimal
result.cpu: Arm Cortex-M33 @ 64 MHz, DSP extension present (libopus ARMv5E paths apply)
result.ram: 211,608 B application RAM (boards/nrf9160dk_nrf9160_ns.overlay); 32 kB secure, modem shares the first 128 kB
result.flash: 1 MB total; application text ~316 kB with libopus at -O3

result.mic: I2S microphone, 15,625 Hz capture, Opus-encoded uplink at 16 kHz / 16 kbps, complexity 0
result.playback: Opus decode on-device at 24 kHz / 60 ms frames, resampled to the 31,250 Hz I2S wire clock, out to the ESP32 bridge
result.codec: libopus 1.6.1 vendored, fixed-point, built -O3. Decode ~25.4 ms per 60 ms packet; encode ~15.0 ms per call. Roughly 87% of one core when both run.

args.model_tier: realtime for initial handoff; cheaper planner/executor for the work and status updates
args.latency_budget: <1s to acknowledge and start; then asynchronous completion with a succinct spoken summary when done
args.cost_estimate: Low at the relay for handoff; cost dominated by Mac/browser execution and any web reads; status checks are cheap
args.security_concerns: Must avoid claiming completion unless the job record says done. Any authenticated content stays on the Mac/browser sessions; only summaries leave.

Reliable status callbacks or a push/queue to notify relay
A spoken summary queue on the pendant or relay for later playback

args.user_asks: “When I’m in a meeting, quietly keep track of decisions and action items, then after it ends tell me only what I personally need to do and put the tasks in the right apps.”
args.why_useful: The pendant is the only node physically present during a meeting, while the Mac and authenticated browser sessions can identify the meeting, relevant documents, and destination task systems. Today the owner must manually record notes and reconstruct commitments afterward.
args.model_tier: Realtime tier only handles a start/stop utterance and urgent spoken feedback; a cheaper background model performs diarization, decision/action extraction, and deduplication; Mac/browser agents execute app writes.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge capture start/stop in under 500 ms; incremental private summaries may arrive every 30–60 seconds; post-meeting result within 2 minutes.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.05–$0.30 per hour depending on audio transcription and summary length; destination writes and browser control dominate latency, not the realtime reply.
args.security_concerns: Meeting audio and transcripts leave the pendant for processing and may contain other people’s confidential information. Store encrypted, retain only extracted commitments by default, visibly indicate capture with the pendant LED, and require explicit spoken confirmation before sending or publishing any task/comment.

A relay background transcription/summarization worker and post-meeting trigger
Meeting identity and document context from Calendar/browser sessions
Typed task/comment destinations plus an approval-aware commit step

args.user_asks: “If something urgent happens in any of my signed-in services, interrupt me on the pendant in the least disruptive way; otherwise hold it and give me one spoken digest when I’m free.”
args.why_useful: The owner is usually away from the Mac, and important events can currently remain trapped in Mail, Calendar, browser tabs, or Mac apps until they manually check each surface. A worn-device arbiter would make urgency actionable without turning every notification into noise.
args.model_tier: Background model classifies and groups events; realtime model is used only to phrase a short interruption and handle the owner’s reply. Deterministic rules handle quiet hours, urgency classes, and deduplication.
args.latency_budget: Urgent event-to-pendant alert under 10 seconds; nonurgent events batched into a digest at the next detected availability window.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per day for event classification and grouping, dominated by polling/webhook volume; speech costs are negligible because alerts are short.
args.security_concerns: The relay would receive metadata from authenticated services and infer availability from audio/device state. Keep content minimization and encrypted per-service tokens, never read message bodies for low-urgency events, provide a physical mute gesture, and make alert policy inspectable and reversible.
missing: A persistent event ingress from Mac and browser sessions (push/webhook or safe polling)
A durable relay queue with urgency grouping, quiet-hours, retry, and deduplication
Pendant push audio/LED notification and a local mute/availability signal
A cross-service policy model that learns the owner’s urgency preferences without exporting raw content

args.why_useful: A worn pendant can remain with the owner in a shop, airport, or appointment where the Mac is absent. The audio bridge supplies the physical conversation path, while the relay can provide low-latency translation and the button can make turn-taking explicit; today the owner needs a phone app and cannot keep the interaction hands-free and discreet.

args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.20–$1.50 per 30-minute conversation depending on streaming audio rates and TTS; bandwidth and continuous audio processing dominate.
args.security_concerns: Nearby people’s speech is sensitive and may be recorded unintentionally. Show active-listening state with LED, use short rolling buffers and delete source audio by default, offer an offline language-pack fallback, and require the button for transmission so the pendant never speaks into a conversation accidentally.

Streaming ASR/translation/TTS with endpointing, echo cancellation, and language switching

args.user_asks: “Screen calls for me: if an unknown caller rings, answer with my short introduction, ask why they’re calling, tell me a one-sentence summary on the pendant, and connect me only when it sounds important.”
args.why_useful: The pendant is the only interface the owner can reliably reach while away from the Mac, yet the Mac/browser may hold contacts, calendars, and call sessions. This would prevent interruptions and spam while preserving urgent human contact; nothing today can combine call audio, identity, conversational triage, and a wearable accept/reject gesture.
args.model_tier: Realtime speech model for call turn-taking and a short spoken summary; cheaper background classification checks contact/calendar context and records a transcript only when configured. Deterministic allow/deny rules should handle known contacts and emergency numbers.
args.latency_budget: Ring-to-screening answer under 2 seconds; caller response latency under 700 ms; owner summary within 3 seconds of the caller’s explanation.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.05–$0.40 per screened call, dominated by telephony audio and realtime model duration; known-contact bypasses are nearly free.
args.security_concerns: This processes private phone audio and could misclassify emergencies or impersonate the owner. Never auto-screen emergency services or allow the system to claim it is the owner; announce an AI receptionist, encrypt/discard recordings by policy, maintain a visible call state, and make connect/reject explicit via the physical button.
missing: Telephony ingress/egress or a Mac phone-call bridge with bidirectional audio
A relay realtime call session manager resilient to handoffs and disconnects
Contact/calendar lookup from the Mac/browser and emergency-number bypass rules
Pendant call-state UX with accept/reject/hang-up and privacy indication

args.change: Add a low-power haptic actuator and a physical three-position privacy switch to the pendant, with firmware events for silent-alert, active-listening, and transmit-disabled states. Expose those states to the relay so every realtime workflow can fail closed when the switch is off and acknowledge urgent events without audio.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can receive a discreet alert in a noisy place and can prove—by touch—that the pendant is not listening or transmitting. This enables safe call screening, meeting capture, and future ambient workflows without forcing the owner to look at a phone or trust an invisible software state.
args.effort: Moderate hardware revision plus GPIO/firmware driver, battery characterization, relay state propagation, and a small set of end-to-end usability tests.
args.risk: Added power draw, enclosure changes, accidental switch movement, and new firmware states. Recover with a default-off transmit state after reboot, watchdog-safe GPIO handling, and a software diagnostic that reports physical switch position.
args.cost_impact: Roughly $2–$8 in components and assembly at prototype quantity; haptic pulses add tens of milliwatts only while active, while the switch is effectively zero draw. No meaningful API cost.
args.latency_impact: Sub-100 ms local haptic response; relay acknowledgement remains network-dependent but is not required for privacy state enforcement.
args.security_impact: Strongly improves privacy by making transmit disable a physical, locally enforced state; switch position must override any server command and be included in audit receipts.
depends_on: A pendant firmware event/state protocol
A relay device-presence and push channel
Audio pipeline session state propagation

The main missing pieces are durable event/audio ingress, background workers, telephony integration, explicit pendant push/state handling, and physical privacy feedback—not another discovery pass.
